SHALL_MANDATORY.meaning: Mandatory requirement established by 'shall' (or explicit prohibition).

DEFAULT_INTERPRETATION.meaning: Default interpretation ('unless otherwise specified' / UOS) flagged when drawing intent may be ambiguous.

rules.section: Foreword & Section 1: Scope, Conventions, and Standard Invocation
rules.title: Prohibition of Concentricity and Symmetry Symbols
rules.audit_check: The drawing SHALL NOT use the eliminated Concentricity (◎) or Symmetry (⌯) geometric characteristic symbols in any Feature Control Frame when ASME Y14.5-2018 is invoked.
rules.pass_condition: Coaxial and symmetrical relationships are controlled exclusively via Position, Profile of a Surface, or Runout tolerances.
rules.fail_condition: A Concentricity (◎) or Symmetry (⌯) symbol appears in any Feature Control Frame on a drawing referencing ASME Y14.5-2018.
rules.remediation: Replace Concentricity with Position (for axis/FOS), Runout (for surface of revolution), or Profile of a Surface; replace Symmetry with Position or Profile of a Surface.

rules.section: Foreword & Section 1: Scope, Conventions, and Standard Invocation
rules.title: Mandatory Standard Designation in Title Block or Notes
rules.audit_check: Engineering documentation based on this Standard SHALL explicitly state the exact designation 'ASME Y14.5-2018' on the drawing/model or in a referenced separate document.
rules.pass_condition: Title block or general notes explicitly cite 'ASME Y14.5-2018' (or reference a controlling document that cites it).
rules.fail_condition: No dimensioning/tolerancing standard is cited, or an undated/ambiguous citation is given without a referenced controlling document.
rules.remediation: Add the note 'INTERPRET DRAWING IN ACCORDANCE WITH ASME Y14.5-2018' in the general notes or title block.

rules.section: Foreword & Section 1: Scope, Conventions, and Standard Invocation
rules.title: Undated Cross-Referenced ASME Y14 Standards
rules.audit_check: Where another ASME Y14 standard is referenced without a revision date, the revision listed in Section 2 of ASME Y14.5-2018 applies by default; where a date is given, ONLY that dated issue shall apply (1.4.2(b)).
rules.pass_condition: Cross-referenced standards either intentionally rely on Section 2 default revisions or explicitly include required revision dates.
rules.fail_condition: Conflicting or ambiguous revision dates appear for referenced ASME Y14 standards.
rules.remediation: Verify whether the Section 2 revision year is intended or explicitly specify the required revision year.

rules.section: Foreword & Section 1: Scope, Conventions, and Standard Invocation
rules.title: Uppercase Convention for Drawing Notes
rules.audit_check: Literal drawing and model note entries (e.g., UOS notes, statistical tolerancing notes, restraint notes) should be presented in ALL UPPERCASE lettering per ASME Y14.2 and Y14.5 conventions.
rules.pass_condition: Drawing and model notes use consistent uppercase lettering (except standardized lowercase symbols such as 'mm').
rules.fail_condition: Drawing notes mix lowercase prose arbitrarily with uppercase entries (excluding lowercase unit symbols like 'mm' or DOF letters [x,y,z,u,v,w]).
rules.remediation: Format literal drawing notes in ALL UPPERCASE lettering while preserving standardized lowercase symbols.

rules.section: Foreword & Section 1: Scope, Conventions, and Standard Invocation
rules.title: Third Angle Projection & Queried Basic Dimensions in 3D Models
rules.audit_check: Multiview orthographic drawings under ASME Y14.5-2018 use third-angle projection by default; in 3D MBD datasets, omitted locating/orienting dimensions are considered basic and SHALL be queried from model geometry.
rules.pass_condition: Drawing uses third-angle projection (or explicitly notes first-angle if deviating) and 3D MBD models clearly specify CAD querying authority.
rules.fail_condition: Projection angle is contradictory between views or 2D orthographic views omit locating dimensions without referencing an authoritative 3D CAD model.
rules.remediation: Confirm third-angle projection symbol in the title block and explicitly cite the authoritative CAD model if dimensions are omitted on 2D views.

rules.section: Foreword & Section 1: Scope, Conventions, and Standard Invocation
rules.title: Mandatory Notation When Using an ASME Y14 Case
rules.audit_check: Where engineering documentation relies on an ASME Y14 Case, that fact SHALL be explicitly noted on the documentation or in a referenced separate document.
rules.pass_condition: Any ASME Y14 Case practices used on the drawing are explicitly cited by Case number in the notes or referenced document.
rules.fail_condition: Non-standard practices permitted only by an ASME Y14 Case are applied without citing the Case.
rules.remediation: Add an explicit general note citing the applicable ASME Y14 Case number.

rules.section: Foreword & Section 1: Scope, Conventions, and Standard Invocation
rules.title: Drawings Without Reference to a Standard Default to ASME PDS-1.1-2013
rules.audit_check: When a drawing omits any reference to a company, regional, national, or international dimensioning standard (or contractual document), it SHALL be interpreted per ASME PDS-1.1-2013 rather than assuming ASME Y14.5-2018 defaults.
rules.pass_condition: Drawing explicitly invokes ASME Y14.5-2018 (or another controlling standard) in its title block or notes.
rules.fail_condition: No standard is referenced anywhere on the drawing while GD&T symbols specific to ASME Y14.5-2018 are used.
rules.remediation: Explicitly invoke ASME Y14.5-2018 in the title block or general notes.

rules.section: Foreword & Section 1: Scope, Conventions, and Standard Invocation
rules.title: Precedence of ASME Y14.5-2018 Text Over Cited Reference Standards
rules.audit_check: In the event of a conflict between the text of ASME Y14.5-2018 and any cited reference standard, the text of ASME Y14.5-2018 SHALL take precedence.
rules.pass_condition: No drawing note contradicts mandatory ASME Y14.5-2018 interpretations via a conflicting secondary standard unless explicitly invoking an exception.
rules.fail_condition: Drawing invokes conflicting tolerancing conventions from secondary reference standards without resolving precedence.
rules.remediation: Align all tolerancing rules with ASME Y14.5-2018 or explicitly document approved exceptions.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Every Feature Shall Be Toleranced
rules.audit_check: Every part feature SHALL have a defined tolerance (direct limit/plus-minus on size, Feature Control Frame for basic definitions, note, or general tolerance block). Basic dimensions SHALL be paired with a Feature Control Frame. Only dimensions explicitly marked as Reference '(...)', MAX, MIN, or commercial STOCK are exempt.
rules.pass_condition: Every non-reference, non-MIN/MAX, non-stock feature is controlled by a direct tolerance, general tolerance block, or FCF (and every basic dimension is tied to an FCF).
rules.fail_condition: Any feature lacks a tolerance, or a Basic Dimension Box appears with no Feature Control Frame governing that feature.
rules.remediation: Apply a direct tolerance, general profile/tolerance note, or Feature Control Frame to every untoleranced feature.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Complete Definition & Prohibition of Scaling or Assumptions
rules.audit_check: Dimensioning and tolerancing SHALL be complete for full understanding of every feature. Scaling directly from a 2D drawing sheet or assuming any distance/size is PROHIBITED (except designated undimensioned drawings such as loft/templates with required control dimensions).
rules.pass_condition: All geometry can be completely defined without scaling the sheet or guessing missing dimensions (or 3D model query authority is stated).
rules.fail_condition: A feature's size, location, or shape is missing from the drawing and cannot be mathematically derived from shown dimensions or an authoritative 3D model.
rules.remediation: Add the missing defining dimension(s) or formally specify an authoritative 3D MBD CAD dataset.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: No Over-Dimensioning (Double Dimensioning) & Minimize Reference Dimensions
rules.audit_check: Each necessary end-product dimension SHALL be shown, and NO MORE dimensions than necessary for complete definition SHALL be given (no closed tolerance chains / redundant double dimensioning). Reference dimensions SHOULD be minimized.
rules.pass_condition: No feature is independently defined twice by conflicting tolerance chains; any redundant informational value is enclosed in parentheses '(...)' and used sparingly.
rules.fail_condition: A closed chain of toleranced dimensions over-constrains a feature, or the same feature dimension is repeated across views without reference parentheses.
rules.remediation: Delete the redundant dimension or convert one non-critical dimension in the chain to a Reference dimension '(...)'.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Unambiguous Functional Dimensioning
rules.audit_check: Dimensions SHALL be selected and arranged to reflect part function and mating relationships and SHALL NOT be subject to more than one interpretation.
rules.pass_condition: Every dimension and tolerance maps unambiguously to its intended feature(s) and functional relationship.
rules.fail_condition: A leader, extension line, note, or tolerance callout can be reasonably interpreted in two or more conflicting ways.
rules.remediation: Re-route leaders/extension lines, add clarifying views or symbols, or replace ambiguous plus/minus dimensions with explicit GD&T controls.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Avoid Specifying Manufacturing Methods Unless Functionally Essential
visual_syntax_triggers: Manufacturing Note (DRILL, REAM, PUNCH, MILL, GRIND)
rules.audit_check: The drawing SHOULD define the finished part geometry without mandating manufacturing processes (e.g., specify hole diameter, not 'DRILL' or 'REAM'). However, where manufacturing, processing, QA, or environmental data IS essential to engineering requirements, it SHALL be specified on the drawing or a referenced document.
rules.pass_condition: Features specify end-state geometry/tolerances without unnecessary process callouts, or essential process specs are formally justified/referenced.
rules.fail_condition: Callouts unnecessarily dictate shop operations (e.g., 'DRILL Ø10.0', 'REAM', 'PUNCH') where only finished geometry matters.
rules.remediation: Remove unnecessary manufacturing process verbs and specify required size, form, position, and surface texture instead.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Labeling Nonmandatory Processing Dimensions
rules.audit_check: Any nonmandatory processing dimensions shown on the drawing (such as finish allowance or shrink allowance) SHALL be explicitly identified with a note such as 'NONMANDATORY (MFG DATA)', provided final dimensions are given.
rules.pass_condition: In-process/allowance dimensions are explicitly tagged 'NONMANDATORY (MFG DATA)' alongside final product dimensions.
rules.fail_condition: In-process or finish-allowance dimensions appear on the drawing without a NONMANDATORY designation.
rules.remediation: Label processing dimensions with 'NONMANDATORY (MFG DATA)' or remove them from the end-product drawing.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Arrange Dimensions for Optimum Readability
rules.audit_check: Dimensions SHOULD be arranged cleanly without overlapping text, obscuring geometry, or crowded callouts to provide optimum readability.
rules.pass_condition: All dimensions, notes, and symbols are legible, well-spaced, and unobstructed.
rules.fail_condition: Dimensions collide with object lines, hatch lines, other dimensions, or FCFs, impairing legibility.
rules.remediation: Re-arrange and space dimensions outside the part outline with clean grouping and alignment.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Dimension to Visible Outlines in True Profile Views
rules.audit_check: In 2D orthographic views, dimensions SHOULD be shown in true profile views and refer to visible outlines (not hidden/dashed lines). In 3D models, dimensions SHALL be applied to show true value (SHALL_MANDATORY for 3D MBD).
rules.pass_condition: Dimensions attach to visible solid outlines in views showing true shape (or section views); 3D model dimensions display true values.
rules.fail_condition: Dimensions are attached to dashed hidden lines or foreshortened views when a true visible/section view is available.
rules.remediation: Move dimensions to a view or section view where the feature appears as a visible outline in true shape.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Linear Dimensions Required for Gage/Code Stock Materials
rules.audit_check: Wires, cables, sheets, rods, and other materials manufactured to gage or code numbers SHALL be specified by linear dimensions indicating diameter or thickness; gage/code numbers may appear only in parentheses following the linear dimension.
rules.pass_condition: Linear thickness/diameter is stated first (e.g., '1.52 (16 GA)'), with gage number optional in parentheses.
rules.fail_condition: Material thickness or diameter is specified solely by a gage/code number (e.g., '16 GA SHEET') with no linear dimension.
rules.remediation: Specify the explicit linear thickness or diameter dimension with tolerance, placing any gage number in parentheses after it.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Implied 90-Degree Angle Default (Non-Basic)
rules.audit_check: An implied 90° angle SHALL apply wherever center lines and lines depicting features are shown at right angles in orthographic views with no angle specified; general angular tolerance applies per 5.1.1.3.
rules.pass_condition: Orthographic right-angle features rely intentionally on the general angular tolerance block (and general angular tolerance is actually stated in the title block).
rules.fail_condition: Implied 90° features exist on a drawing that has NO general angular tolerance specified in the title block or notes.
rules.remediation: Ensure a general angular tolerance is specified in the title block or apply explicit geometric orientation tolerances.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Implied 90-Degree Basic Angle Default
rules.audit_check: An implied 90° BASIC angle SHALL apply where center lines of features or surfaces shown at right angles on an orthographic view are located or defined by basic dimensions and no angle is specified; governed by the applicable FCF per 5.1.1.4.
rules.pass_condition: Implied 90° basic relationships are controlled by an FCF (position, orientation, profile, or runout).
rules.fail_condition: Features defined by basic dimensions at implied 90° lack an applicable FCF governing their orientation/location.
rules.remediation: Verify an FCF governs all features related by implied 90° basic angles.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Implied Zero Basic Dimension for Coincident Features
rules.audit_check: A zero basic dimension SHALL apply where axes, center planes, or surfaces are shown coincident on orthographic views (or queried as zero on CAD models) and geometric tolerances establish the relationship between the features.
rules.pass_condition: Coincident axes/planes/surfaces have an FCF (position, profile, or runout) controlling their mutual relationship.
rules.fail_condition: Coaxial diameters or coplanar/symmetrical surfaces are shown coincident with NO geometric tolerance establishing their coaxiality, symmetry, or coplanarity.
rules.remediation: Apply a Position, Runout, or Profile FCF to govern the coincident relationship.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Standard Reference Temperature Default (20°C / 68°F)
rules.audit_check: UOS, all dimensions and tolerances apply at 20°C (68°F) per ASME B89.6.2.
rules.pass_condition: Inspection at 20°C (68°F) is appropriate, or an alternate reference temperature is explicitly stated in the general notes.
rules.fail_condition: Drawing implies a non-standard inspection temperature (e.g., cryogenic/elevated service) without specifying an explicit temperature override note.
rules.remediation: Add an explicit reference temperature note if dimensions must be verified at other than 20°C (68°F).

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Free State Inspection Default
rules.audit_check: UOS, all dimensions and tolerances apply in a free-state (unrestrained) condition. Non-rigid parts requiring restraint during inspection must invoke a restraint note per subsection 7.20.
rules.pass_condition: Part is evaluated free-state by default, OR a formal restraint note specifies clamping/restraint conditions and any free-state exceptions use Ⓕ.
rules.fail_condition: A Free State symbol Ⓕ is used on a drawing that has NO restraint note (redundant/invalid per 7.20.4), or a thin flexible part has tight flatness/profile tolerances with ambiguous restraint intent.
rules.remediation: Remove Ⓕ if no restraint note exists, or add a complete restraint note per 7.20.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Full Depth, Length, and Width Default for Tolerances and Datums
rules.audit_check: UOS, all geometric tolerances and datum features apply for the FULL depth, length, and width of the feature.
rules.pass_condition: Full-extent application matches functional intent, or limited extent is explicitly bounded by a chain line, datum targets, or 'between' symbol.
rules.fail_condition: A datum feature or tolerance appears intended for only a portion of a surface without a chain line, 'between' symbol, or note limiting its extent.
rules.remediation: Add a dimensioned chain line (4.4.3), datum target area, or 'between' symbol (6.3.11) if partial-surface control is intended.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Drawing-Level Applicability of Dimensions and Tolerances
rules.audit_check: Dimensions and tolerances apply ONLY at the drawing level where specified (a detail-drawing requirement is not automatically mandatory at an assembly drawing level unless re-specified).
rules.pass_condition: Post-assembly critical features (e.g., welded/pressed assemblies) have their required tolerances explicitly restated on the assembly drawing.
rules.fail_condition: Assembly drawing assumes detail-level tolerances survive welding/pressing without re-specifying assembly-level requirements.
rules.remediation: Specify required post-assembly dimensions and geometric tolerances directly on the assembly drawing.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: As-Designed Value Is Not a Manufacturing/Functional Target
rules.audit_check: UOS by a drawing/model note or separate document, the as-designed (nominal/basic) dimension value does NOT establish a functional or manufacturing target.
rules.pass_condition: Any value within specified limits is acceptable, or an explicit target/SPC note is added when centering is functionally required.
rules.fail_condition: Design requires targeting a specific nominal value (e.g., for Cpk/SPC) without a drawing note or referenced specification.
rules.remediation: Add an explicit target or statistical tolerancing specification (5.18) if a target value is required.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Right-Handed Coordinate System with Labeled Positive Axes
rules.audit_check: Where a coordinate system is shown on orthographic views or in a model, it SHALL be right-handed UOS, each axis SHALL be labeled (X, Y, Z), and the positive direction SHALL be shown. (Note: Model coordinate systems shown on drawings SHALL comply with ASME Y14.41.)
rules.pass_condition: Displayed coordinate triad follows the right-hand rule (X × Y = Z) with every axis labeled and arrowheads showing positive directions.
rules.fail_condition: Coordinate triad is left-handed without explicit UOS override, omits axis labels, or omits positive direction arrowheads.
rules.remediation: Correct the coordinate triad to right-handed orientation and add X, Y, Z labels with positive direction arrows.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Surface Texture and Flaws Included Within Tolerance Zone
rules.audit_check: UOS, elements of a surface include surface texture and flaws (e.g., burrs and scratches), and ALL elements of a surface SHALL lie within the applicable specified tolerance zone boundaries.
rules.pass_condition: Surface finish roughness/waviness values are compatible with (smaller than) geometric/size tolerance zones, or exceptions are noted.
rules.fail_condition: Specified surface texture/flaw allowance is incompatible with or contradictory to a tighter geometric tolerance zone without clarification.
rules.remediation: Verify surface texture callouts are consistent with dimensional/geometric tolerance zones and specify burr/edge-break notes clearly.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Mandatory Linear Unit Identification Note
visual_syntax_triggers: ALL DIMENSIONS ARE IN MILLIMETERS / INCHES
rules.audit_check: Every single-unit drawing SHALL contain an explicit note stating 'UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED, ALL DIMENSIONS ARE IN MILLIMETERS' or 'IN INCHES' (as applicable).
rules.pass_condition: Title block or general notes unambiguously state whether linear dimensions are in MILLIMETERS or INCHES.
rules.fail_condition: Linear units (mm vs. in) are completely omitted from both the title block and general notes.
rules.remediation: Add 'UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED, ALL DIMENSIONS ARE IN MILLIMETERS' (or 'IN INCHES') to the title block or general notes.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Mixed Metric and Inch Unit Suffix Identification
rules.audit_check: Where inch dimensions appear on a millimeter-dimensioned drawing, 'IN' SHALL follow each inch value; where millimeter dimensions appear on an inch-dimensioned drawing, 'mm' SHALL follow each millimeter value.
rules.pass_condition: Every secondary-unit dimension is explicitly suffixed with 'IN' (on metric drawings) or 'mm' (on inch drawings).
rules.fail_condition: A secondary-unit dimension (e.g., an inch fastener/stock callout on a metric drawing) omits the 'IN' or 'mm' suffix.
rules.remediation: Append 'IN' to inch dimensions on metric drawings and 'mm' to metric dimensions on inch drawings.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Angular Unit Formatting & Leading Zeros for Angles Less Than 1°
rules.audit_check: Angular dimensions SHALL use °, ′, and " symbols. Values expressed only in degrees SHALL include °; values < 1° in minutes/seconds SHALL be preceded by 0° or 0°0′; decimal angles < 1° SHALL include a leading zero (e.g., 0.5°, NOT .5°).
rules.pass_condition: All angular dimensions include ° (and ′ / " where used) and include leading 0°/0°0′ or 0. for values under 1°.
rules.fail_condition: An angular value < 1° omits the leading zero (e.g., '.5°' or '30′' without '0°'), or a degree value omits '°'.
rules.remediation: Format sub-degree angles as '0.5°', '0°30′', or '0°0′15"' and ensure '°' follows all degree numerals.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Decimal Dimensioning Required (No Fractions Except Standardized Commodities)
rules.audit_check: Decimal dimensioning SHALL be used on drawings; fractional dimensions are prohibited except for commercial commodities identified by standardized nominal designations (e.g., pipe sizes, lumber, unified fractional thread callouts).
rules.pass_condition: All part feature dimensions are expressed in decimals (with fractions limited strictly to standardized commercial nominal designations).
rules.fail_condition: Fractional dimensions (e.g., '3/4', '1-1/8') are used to dimension machined or molded part geometry.
rules.remediation: Convert fractional feature dimensions to decimal inch or millimeter values.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Millimeter Dimensions < 1 mm Require Leading Zero
rules.audit_check: For millimeter dimensions (and tolerances) less than 1 mm, a leading zero SHALL precede the decimal point (e.g., '0.9', NOT '.9').
rules.pass_condition: Every metric value less than 1 mm displays a leading zero before the decimal point (e.g., 0.25, 0.05).
rules.fail_condition: Any metric dimension or FCF tolerance value < 1 mm omits the leading zero (e.g., '.5', '±.1', '|⌖|Ø.05|A|').
rules.remediation: Insert a leading zero before the decimal point on all metric values less than 1 mm.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Whole-Number Millimeter Dimensions Omit Decimal Point and Trailing Zero
rules.audit_check: Where a millimeter dimension is a whole number, NEITHER a decimal point NOR a trailing zero SHALL be shown (e.g., '12', NOT '12.0' or '12.00'), except where required for limit/bilateral tolerance matching per 5.3.1(b)-(c).
rules.pass_condition: Whole-number metric nominal/basic dimensions are shown without decimal point or trailing zeros (e.g., 25, 100).
rules.fail_condition: Whole-number metric nominal or basic dimensions display trailing zeros (e.g., '25.0', '10.00' on a non-limit dimension).
rules.remediation: Remove unnecessary decimal points and trailing zeros from whole-number metric nominal/basic dimensions.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: No Trailing Zero on Fractional Millimeter Dimensions
rules.audit_check: Where a millimeter dimension exceeds a whole number by a decimal fraction, the last digit to the right of the decimal point SHALL NOT be followed by a trailing zero (e.g., '12.5', NOT '12.50'), except for bilateral tolerances or limit dimensions per 5.3.1(b)-(c).
rules.pass_condition: Fractional metric nominal/basic dimensions trim trailing zeros (e.g., 12.5, 6.25).
rules.fail_condition: Fractional metric nominal/basic dimensions include unnecessary trailing zeros (e.g., '12.50', '6.20').
rules.remediation: Remove trailing zeros from fractional metric nominal/basic dimensions (retaining matched decimals only inside bilateral/limit tolerance pairs).

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: No Commas or Spaces as Thousands Separators in Millimeter Dimensions
rules.audit_check: Neither commas NOR spaces SHALL be used to separate digits into groups in millimeter dimensions (e.g., '1250', NOT '1,250' or '1 250').
rules.pass_condition: All multi-digit metric dimensions >= 1000 are written as continuous digits without commas or spaces.
rules.fail_condition: A comma or space separates digit groups in a millimeter dimension (e.g., '1,500' or '2 000').
rules.remediation: Remove all commas and group-separator spaces from millimeter dimensions.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Decimal Inch Dimensions < 1 in Omit Leading Zero
rules.audit_check: On decimal-inch drawings, a leading zero SHALL NOT be used before the decimal point for values less than 1 inch (e.g., '.500', NOT '0.500').
rules.pass_condition: Every decimal inch dimension and tolerance value < 1 in begins directly with the decimal point (e.g., .250, ±.005).
rules.fail_condition: Any decimal inch dimension or FCF tolerance value < 1 in displays a leading zero (e.g., '0.250', '±0.005').
rules.remediation: Remove leading zeros from all decimal inch values less than 1 inch.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Decimal Inch Dimension Matches Tolerance Decimal Places
rules.audit_check: On decimal-inch drawings, a directly toleranced dimension SHALL be expressed to the exact same number of decimal places as its tolerance, adding trailing zeros to the right of the decimal point where necessary (e.g., '1.500 ±.005', NOT '1.5 ±.005').
rules.pass_condition: Nominal inch dimension and its associated tolerance have identical decimal-place counts (except basic dimensions per 5.3.2(d)).
rules.fail_condition: An inch dimension has fewer or more decimal places than its directly applied tolerance (e.g., '.5 ±.005' or '2.00 ±.010').
rules.remediation: Pad the inch dimension with trailing zeros (or align tolerance precision) so dimension and tolerance share identical decimal places.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Decimal Point Legibility and Baseline Alignment
rules.audit_check: Decimal points SHALL be uniform, dense, clearly visible for reproduction, and aligned with the bottom baseline of the associated digits.
rules.pass_condition: All decimal points are crisp, unmistakable, and baseline-aligned.
rules.fail_condition: Decimal points are faint, dropped, ambiguous, or mid-height centered dots.
rules.remediation: Use standard ASME Y14.2 lettering with bold, baseline-aligned decimal points.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Unit Conversion and Rounding Default (IEEE/ASTM SI 10)
rules.audit_check: UOS, conversion and rounding between SI and U.S. Customary linear units SHALL follow IEEE/ASTM SI 10. Dual dimensions (if present) should be checked for non-conflicting rounded limits.
rules.pass_condition: Single-unit system is used cleanly, or any unit conversion notes follow IEEE/ASTM SI 10 without contradictory limits.
rules.fail_condition: Dual-dimensioned tolerances display mathematically conflicting rounded limits between metric and inch equivalents.
rules.remediation: Use a single linear unit system (preferred) or verify conversions strictly per IEEE/ASTM SI 10.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Dimension Line Break & Forbidden Line Substitutions
rules.audit_check: A center line, extension line, phantom line, object outline, or continuation of any of these lines SHALL NOT be used as a dimension line (4.4.1 Note). Dimension lines SHOULD be broken for numeral insertion (or numerals placed above unbroken horizontal lines).
rules.pass_condition: All dimension lines are dedicated thin lines with arrowheads, never borrowing object outlines, center lines, extension lines, or phantom lines.
rules.fail_condition: Arrowheads are placed directly on an object edge, center line, phantom line, or extension line used as a dimension line.
rules.remediation: Draw dedicated dimension lines offset from the part outline and never reuse object, center, phantom, or extension lines as dimension lines.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Alignment and Grouping of Dimension Lines
rules.audit_check: Related dimension lines SHOULD be aligned and grouped for uniform appearance; parallel dimension values SHOULD be staggered where closely spaced (4.4.1.2).
rules.pass_condition: Dimension lines are neatly aligned, spaced adequately from the part outline (≥10 mm first line, ≥6 mm subsequent lines), and staggered where stacked.
rules.fail_condition: Dimension lines are erratically staggered, cramped against the part outline, or have stacked colliding numerals.
rules.remediation: Align related chain/baseline dimension lines and maintain minimum standard spacing.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Avoid Crossing Dimension Lines; Keep Unavoidable Crossings Unbroken
rules.audit_check: Crossing dimension lines SHOULD be avoided. Where crossing dimension lines is unavoidable, the dimension lines SHALL remain unbroken.
rules.pass_condition: Dimension lines do not cross, or any unavoidable crossing keeps both dimension lines continuous and unbroken.
rules.fail_condition: A dimension line is broken solely where it crosses another dimension line.
rules.remediation: Re-order dimensions (shortest closest to outline) to avoid crossings, or keep unavoidable crossing dimension lines unbroken.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Extension Line Gap, Projection, and Oblique Orientation
rules.audit_check: Extension lines start with a short visible gap from the part outline and extend past the outermost dimension line. Where oblique extension lines are used for limited space, the dimension lines SHALL still be shown in the direction in which they apply.
rules.pass_condition: Extension lines show clean gaps from outlines, extend past dimension arrowheads, and any oblique extension lines pair with properly oriented dimension lines.
rules.fail_condition: Oblique extension lines are paired with a tilted dimension line not aligned to the measurement direction, or extension lines merge seamlessly into object lines causing confusion.
rules.remediation: Maintain visible gaps at part outlines and keep dimension lines parallel to the actual measurement direction.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Extension Line Crossings and Shortest-Inside Ordering
rules.audit_check: Extension lines SHOULD NOT cross each other or dimension lines; the shortest dimension line should be placed nearest the part outline. Unavoidable crossings are not broken except permissibly near arrowheads.
rules.pass_condition: Shortest dimensions sit closest to the part outline, minimizing crossings, and crossing extension lines remain unbroken away from arrowheads.
rules.fail_condition: Longer dimensions are placed inside shorter dimensions causing avoidable dimension/extension line crossings.
rules.remediation: Re-order parallel dimensions from shortest (nearest outline) to longest (outermost).

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Limited Length or Area Indication via Chain Line & Hatching (4.4.3.1–4.4.3.3)
rules.audit_check: Where a limited length/area receives special treatment or tolerance: (4.4.3.1) draw a thick chain line parallel to the surface profile at a short offset with length/location dimensions (one side only is acceptable on surfaces of revolution); (4.4.3.3) on a direct view of the surface, section-line (hatch) inside the chain-line boundary and dimension it. On 3D models, use supplemental geometry.
rules.pass_condition: Limited-area treatments use properly offset chain lines (or hatched chain boundaries in direct views) with clear location/extent dimensions unless visually self-evident (4.4.3.2).
rules.fail_condition: A limited-area surface treatment or partial tolerance uses an arbitrary dashed/solid line or omits location/length dimensions where boundaries are ambiguous.
rules.remediation: Indicate limited surface zones with a standard thick chain line (plus section lines in direct views) and clear locating/length dimensions.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Leader Line Termination (Arrowhead vs. Dot) and Geometry
rules.audit_check: When a leader refers to a surface by ending WITHIN the outline of that surface, the leader SHALL terminate in a dot (not an arrowhead). Leaders to edges/outlines terminate in an arrowhead. Leaders SHOULD be inclined straight lines with a short horizontal shoulder extending to the midheight of the first or last character; radial leaders SHOULD be used on circles/arcs (4.4.4.2).
rules.pass_condition: Leaders ending inside a surface outline use a dot; leaders to edges/holes use an arrowhead; circular leaders point radially toward center.
rules.fail_condition: A leader ending inside a surface outline uses an arrowhead instead of a dot, or a leader pointing to an edge/hole terminates in a dot.
rules.remediation: Change the termination to a dot when landing inside a surface outline, or move an arrowhead leader to terminate cleanly on an edge/outline.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Individual Leader-Directed Dimensions & Feature Lettering When Crowded
rules.audit_check: Leader-directed dimensions are specified individually to avoid complicated/crossing leaders. Where numerous leaders would impair legibility, identifying letters or symbols in a hole chart/legend SHOULD be used instead.
rules.pass_condition: Leaders are clean, parallel where adjacent, and uncrossed; dense hole fields use a hole table or feature letters.
rules.fail_condition: Tangled or crossing leaders obscure geometry or make hole-to-callout mapping error-prone.
rules.remediation: Replace dense crossing leaders with feature identification letters and a tabular hole chart.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Unidirectional Reading Direction from Bottom of Drawing
rules.audit_check: Notes (4.4.5.1), dimensions with dimension lines (4.4.5.2), Feature Control Frames (4.4.5.4), and Datum Feature Symbols (4.4.5.5) SHOULD be oriented horizontally to read from the bottom of the drawing (unidirectional). Baseline/ordinate dimensions without dimension lines SHOULD read from the bottom or right side (4.4.5.3).
rules.pass_condition: All notes, linear dimensions, FCFs, and datum feature letters read horizontally from the bottom of the sheet.
rules.fail_condition: Feature Control Frames, datum letters, or standard dimensions are rotated sideways/upside-down (except ordinate/baseline aligned right-reading values).
rules.remediation: Orient notes, dimensions, FCFs, and datum feature frames horizontally to read from the bottom of the drawing.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Reference Dimension Parentheses & Overall Dimension Omission (4.4.7)
rules.audit_check: Reference dimensions on drawings are enclosed in parentheses '(...)'. When an overall dimension is specified, one intermediate dimension is omitted or marked as reference '(...)'; when intermediate dimensions control, the overall dimension (if shown) is marked as reference '(...)' (4.4.7).
rules.pass_condition: Reference dimensions use parentheses '(...)' (not legacy 'REF' on graphics) and no overall + complete intermediate chain is doubly toleranced.
rules.fail_condition: Overall dimension and all intermediate dimensions in a chain are toleranced simultaneously without omitting or parenthesizing one.
rules.remediation: Enclose the non-governing overall or intermediate dimension in parentheses '(...)' or delete it.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Place Dimensions Outside View Outlines Unless Clarity Requires Placement Inside
rules.audit_check: Dimensions SHOULD normally be placed outside the outline of a view. Placement inside a view is acceptable only where directness improves clarity or avoids excessively long extension/leader lines (and section hatching should be broken around any internal text).
rules.pass_condition: Dimensions sit outside part outlines wherever practical; any internal dimensions are clear of hatching and object edges.
rules.fail_condition: Dimensions are unnecessarily crowded inside the part outline or written directly over unbroken section hatching.
rules.remediation: Move dimensions outside the view outline or break section hatching cleanly behind unavoidable internal dimensions.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Out-of-Scale Dimensions Underlined on Hard-Copy Drawings
rules.audit_check: Pictorial representation SHOULD agree with defining dimensions. When a hard-copy drawing dimension is out of scale and cannot be redrawn, the out-of-scale dimension SHALL be underlined with a straight thick line (placed beneath the frame if it is a basic dimension).
rules.pass_condition: Feature proportions match stated dimensions, or any intentionally out-of-scale hard-copy dimension is properly underlined with a straight thick line.
rules.fail_condition: A dimension visibly contradicts view proportions (e.g., edited value without updating geometry) and lacks an out-of-scale underline.
rules.remediation: Update the view geometry to true scale or underline the out-of-scale dimension with a straight thick line.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Mandatory Diameter Symbol (Ø / SØ) Preceding All Diameter Values
rules.audit_check: The diameter symbol 'Ø' SHALL precede ALL diameter values (and 'SØ' for spherical diameters), with no space between symbol and value (6.3.7). Concentric cylindrical diameters SHOULD be dimensioned in a longitudinal view.
rules.pass_condition: Every cylindrical and spherical diameter value is preceded directly by 'Ø' or 'SØ' (e.g., Ø12.5, SØ20) with no space.
rules.fail_condition: A diameter dimension omits 'Ø'/'SØ', uses legacy suffix 'DIA', or inserts a space between 'Ø' and the numeral.
rules.remediation: Precede every diameter value directly with 'Ø' (or 'SØ' for spheres) with zero intervening space.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Radius Symbol (R / CR / SR), Single Arrowhead, and Unlocated Center Prohibition
rules.audit_check: Each radius value SHALL be preceded by R, CR, or SR (4.5.2.5 for spherical radii) with no space. A radius dimension line uses ONLY ONE arrowhead at the arc end (NEVER an arrowhead at the center). Where the radius center is NOT dimensionally located, the center SHALL NOT be indicated (4.5.2); where located, extension/dimension lines SHALL locate the center with a small cross (4.5.2.1); where unlocated, tangent/adjacent controlling geometry SHALL be clear (4.5.2.1). Radius dimension lines SHALL NOT be foreshortened on 3D models (4.5.2.2).
rules.pass_condition: Radii use R/CR/SR prefix, single arrowhead at the arc, omit center crosses when unlocated, and clearly locate centers when controlled.
rules.fail_condition: Radius omits R/CR/SR prefix, places an arrowhead at the arc center, shows a center cross for an unlocated tangent radius, or foreshortens a radius in a 3D model.
rules.remediation: Prefix with R/CR/SR, use a single arrowhead touching the arc, and remove center marks for unlocated radii.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: 'TRUE' Qualifier for Foreshortened Orthographic Features (Not Allowed on 3D Models)
rules.audit_check: On a 2D orthographic view where a radius (or other feature) is dimensioned in a view not showing its true shape, 'TRUE' is added before or after the dimension. This practice is NOT applicable (prohibited) on 3D models.
rules.pass_condition: Foreshortened 2D radii include 'TRUE' (or are moved to a true-shape view); 3D models never use 'TRUE'.
rules.fail_condition: A foreshortened 2D radius omits 'TRUE', or a 3D model dimension includes 'TRUE'.
rules.remediation: Dimension in a true-shape view, add 'TRUE' on foreshortened 2D views only, and remove 'TRUE' from 3D models.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Chords, Arcs, Rounded Corners, and Symmetrical Outlines (4.5.3, 4.5.5, 4.5.9)
visual_syntax_triggers: Part Symmetry Symbol (‖ on Center Line)
rules.audit_check: Chords and arcs SHALL be dimensioned distinctively per Figure 4-26 (chord with straight dimension line; arc length with curved dimension line and arc symbol above value). Where corners are rounded (4.5.5), dimensions define sharp-corner edge intersections and arcs are tangent. Where a half-view shows a symmetrical outline on a 2D sheet (4.5.9), ASME Y14.2 part symmetry symbols SHALL be applied to the center line.
rules.pass_condition: Arcs carry the arc-length symbol above the dimension; half-views carry symmetry symbols on the centerline.
rules.fail_condition: An arc length dimension omits the arc-length symbol (looking like an angle or chord), or a half-symmetrical view omits ASME Y14.2 symmetry marks.
rules.remediation: Add the arc-length symbol above arc dimensions and apply ASME Y14.2 symmetry symbols to half-view centerlines.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Rounded Ends and Slotted Holes — Do Not Dimension Full End Radii
rules.audit_check: For features with fully rounded ends (including slotted holes), the end radii are indicated with 'R' ONLY (NOT given a toleranced numeric value that would over-constrain the width), whereas partially rounded ends have their radii dimensioned.
rules.pass_condition: Fully rounded slots specify width and overall/center-to-center length with an unvalued 'R' (or reference radius), avoiding over-dimensioning.
rules.fail_condition: A fully rounded slot specifies both a toleranced width (e.g., 10 ±0.1) AND a toleranced end radius (e.g., 2X R5 ±0.1), creating a double-dimension conflict.
rules.remediation: Replace the redundant numeric radius on fully rounded ends with 'R' (or '2X R' / '(R5)' reference).

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Round Holes — THRU Notation and Blind Hole Depth Interpretation
rules.audit_check: If it is not visually clear that a hole goes completely through, 'THRU' follows the dimension. Blind-hole depth applies to the FULL diameter from the outer surface; where outer-surface depth is unclear (e.g., curved surface), depth SHOULD be shown with dimension/extension lines rather than a note.
rules.pass_condition: Through holes clearly show through-extent or 'THRU'; blind hole depth on curved surfaces is explicitly dimensioned with extension/dimension lines.
rules.fail_condition: Hole extent (blind vs. through) is ambiguous, or a depth-symbol note on a curved surface leaves the measurement origin ambiguous.
rules.remediation: Add 'THRU' where unclear, and use explicit dimension/extension lines for blind depths originating from curved surfaces.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Counterbored Holes — Coaxial Relationship Must Be Specified
rules.audit_check: Counterbored holes specify diameter and depth (or remaining material thickness). The geometric relationship (coaxiality/position) between the counterbore and the through/pilot hole SHALL be specified (e.g., single FCF below both callouts or individual FCFs per 10.4.2).
rules.pass_condition: Counterbore diameter, depth/remaining thickness, and coaxial/positional relationship to the hole are all explicitly specified.
rules.fail_condition: Counterbore is dimensioned for size and depth only, with no FCF or control establishing its coaxiality to the mating hole.
rules.remediation: Apply a shared Position FCF beneath the hole/counterbore callout or separate FCFs per 10.4.2.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Countersunk Holes, Counterdrilled Holes, and Curved-Surface Countersinks (4.5.13)
rules.audit_check: Countersinks specify diameter and included angle (or gage diameter/depth). On a curved surface (4.5.13), the specified diameter applies at the MINOR diameter of the chamfer or countersink. Counterdrill depth applies to the full diameter from the outer surface.
rules.pass_condition: Countersink specifies diameter + included angle (with tolerance), and curved-surface countersink callouts reflect minor-diameter interpretation.
rules.fail_condition: Countersink omits either the diameter or included angle, or fails to account for curved-surface minor-diameter interpretation.
rules.remediation: Specify both countersink diameter and included angle with tolerances, clarifying gage diameter if needed on curved surfaces.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Spotface Default Depth & Diameter Across Flat
rules.audit_check: If no depth or remaining thickness is specified for a spotface, the default is the MINIMUM depth necessary to clean up the surface to the specified diameter. The spotface diameter is measured across the FLAT only (excluding any corner fillet).
rules.pass_condition: Spotface specifies diameter (and optional depth/remaining thickness, fillet radius, and target surface if on a through hole).
rules.fail_condition: Spotface on a through-hole fails to identify which face receives the spotface, or implies diameter includes the fillet.
rules.remediation: Clarify which surface is spotfaced on through-holes and add depth/remaining thickness if functional cleanup depth matters.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Chamfer-by-Note Restricted Strictly to 45° Chamfers on Perpendicular Surfaces
rules.audit_check: Note-style chamfer callouts (e.g., '2 X 45°') are permitted ONLY for 45° chamfers between perpendicular surfaces (because the linear leg applies equally in either direction). Non-45° chamfers or chamfers on non-perpendicular surfaces SHALL be dimensioned explicitly by angle + linear leg from an indicated surface, or two linear dimensions (4.5.16, 4.5.16.3).
rules.pass_condition: Note-format chamfer callouts are used exclusively for 45° chamfers on 90° corners; all other chamfers show explicit geometry/direction.
rules.fail_condition: A note format such as '2 X 30°' is used without graphically indicating which leg carries the linear dimension.
rules.remediation: Dimension non-45° chamfers directly with extension/dimension lines showing the angle and the specific linear distance from the indicated surface.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Keyseat Complete Definition (Width, Depth, Location, Length) & Machining Centers (4.5.15)
rules.audit_check: Keyseats are dimensioned by width, depth (preferably from the opposite side of the shaft or bore to aid inspection), location, and length if required (4.5.17). Machining centers intended to remain on the finished part are indicated by note or dimension per ASME B94.11M (4.5.15).
rules.pass_condition: Keyseats specify width, inspectable depth, axial/angular location, and length; retained center holes are explicitly specified.
rules.fail_condition: Keyseat depth is dimensioned from a non-existent theoretical cylinder edge intersection without clarity, or omits width/length/location.
rules.remediation: Dimension keyseat depth from the opposite side of the shaft/bore and specify width, location, and length.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Knurling — Partial Length/Location & Press-Fit Specification (4.5.18.1)
rules.audit_check: Where only a portion of a feature is knurled, location and length SHALL be specified. For press-fit knurls (4.5.18.1), a note SHALL specify knurl type, pitch, toleranced diameter BEFORE knurling, and minimum acceptable diameter AFTER knurling.
rules.pass_condition: Partial knurls are located and length-dimensioned; press-fit knurls specify type, pitch, pre-knurl toleranced diameter, and post-knurl minimum diameter.
rules.fail_condition: Partial knurl lacks length/location dimensions, or press-fit knurl omits pre-knurl diameter or post-knurl minimum diameter.
rules.remediation: Add complete knurl type, pitch, extent dimensions, and before/after diameters where applicable.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Identification of Datum, DRF, or Origin Features for Location Dimensions
rules.audit_check: The part features that establish the datum, datum reference frame, or origin for rectangular (4.6.1) or polar (4.6.4) coordinate locating dimensions SHALL be clearly identified.
rules.pass_condition: All locating dimensions trace clearly back to identified datum features, a DRF, or explicit origin planes.
rules.fail_condition: Coordinate locating dimensions float from an unidentified edge/centerline or fail to identify which part features establish the coordinate planes.
rules.remediation: Identify the originating features with Datum Feature Symbols (and reference them in FCFs) or explicit origin planes.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Ordinate (Baseline Without Dimension Lines) Zero Coordinate Indicators & Tabular Dimensioning (4.6.3)
rules.audit_check: Where rectangular coordinate (ordinate) dimensioning without dimension lines is used (4.6.2), each base line SHALL be clearly indicated as a zero coordinate ('0') tied to an identified origin/datum feature. Where tabular coordinate dimensioning is used (4.6.3), all feature IDs on the view SHALL match rows in the coordinate table with identified X, Y, (Z) origin planes.
rules.pass_condition: Every ordinate dimension series starts at a clearly labeled '0' origin on an identified part feature/datum; tabular IDs match view labels 1-to-1.
rules.fail_condition: Ordinate dimensions omit the '0' base-line indicator, or tabular hole labels on the drawing are missing/mismatched in the table.
rules.remediation: Label every ordinate baseline '0' on its physical origin feature and audit 1-to-1 correspondence between view labels and coordinate tables.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: Repetitive Feature 'X' Syntax — No Space Before 'X', One Space After 'X'
rules.audit_check: For repetitive features or equal spacing (4.6.5.1, 4.6.5.2), NO space is used between the numeral and 'X', and ONE space is used between 'X' and the dimension (e.g., '4X Ø10', NOT '4 X Ø10' or '4XØ10'). With a basic dimension, '4X' may be placed inside or outside the basic box.
rules.pass_condition: All repetitive feature counts use '<N>X <dimension>' formatting (e.g., '6X Ø8.5', '4X 25').
rules.fail_condition: Space is inserted before 'X' (e.g., '4 X Ø10') or omitted after 'X' (e.g., '4XØ10'), or legacy '4 PLACES'/'TYP' is ambiguously used where exact count is needed.
rules.remediation: Format repetitive feature counts strictly as '<N>X <value>' with no space before X and one space after X.

rules.section: Section 4: Fundamental Rules, Tolerancing Defaults, and Dimensioning Practices
rules.title: 'X' Meaning 'By' Syntax — One Space Before and After 'X' (and Disambiguation Note)
rules.audit_check: Where 'X' indicates 'by' between coordinate dimensions (e.g., '2 X 45°' or '25 X 25'), 'X' SHALL be preceded AND followed by one character space. (4.6.6 Note: When both 'places' (4.6.5) and 'by' (4.6.6) appear on the same drawing, care SHALL be taken to ensure each usage is unmistakable, e.g., '4X 2 X 45°'.)
rules.pass_condition: 'By' expressions include one space on both sides of 'X', cleanly distinguished from '<N>X ' quantity prefixes.
rules.fail_condition: Spaces around 'by' X are omitted (e.g., '2X45°' reading ambiguously as two 45° features instead of a 2 by 45° chamfer).
rules.remediation: Insert one space before and after 'X' when meaning 'by' (e.g., '2 X 45°') and ensure unambiguous separation from count prefixes.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Use Positional Tolerancing for FOS Location & Profile for Irregular Shapes
rules.audit_check: Location of regular features of size (holes, pins, slots, tabs) uses Positional Tolerancing (Section 10); location of irregular shaped features SHOULD use Profile Tolerancing (Section 11). Direct plus/minus location tolerances on regular features of size have NO defined meaning in ASME Y14.5-2018 (see Mandatory Appendix I-2).
rules.pass_condition: All regular features of size are located with basic dimensions and Position FCFs; irregular features are located with Profile FCFs.
rules.fail_condition: Plus/minus tolerances are directly applied to coordinate dimensions locating holes, bosses, or slots.
rules.remediation: Convert location dimensions for features of size to basic dimensions and control location with a Position FCF.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Basic Dimension Identification & Prohibition of General ± Tolerance Block with 'UNTOLERANCED DIMENSIONS ARE BASIC'
rules.audit_check: Basic dimensions SHALL be indicated by: (a) enclosing each in a basic rectangle, (b) a general note such as 'UNTOLERANCED DIMENSIONS ARE BASIC', (c) implied 0°/90° basic angles, or (d) querying a 3D model. CRITICAL NOTE (5.1.1.2(b) Note): When using 'UNTOLERANCED DIMENSIONS ARE BASIC', a general plus/minus tolerance block or note IS NOT ALLOWED on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Basic dimensions use boxes or an 'UNTOLERANCED DIMENSIONS ARE BASIC' note, AND if the note is used, no general ± linear/angular tolerance block remains active on the drawing.
rules.fail_condition: The drawing states 'UNTOLERANCED DIMENSIONS ARE BASIC' while ALSO retaining an active title-block general plus/minus tolerance table (e.g., .XX ±.01), creating a fatal conflict.
rules.remediation: Strike/remove the general plus/minus tolerance block whenever 'UNTOLERANCED DIMENSIONS ARE BASIC' is invoked, and specify a general profile tolerance instead.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Limit Dimensioning Ordering (High Over Low / Low-Dash-High)
rules.audit_check: In stacked limit dimensioning, the HIGH limit (maximum value) is placed ABOVE the low limit (minimum value). When written on a single line, the LOW limit precedes the high limit separated by a dash (e.g., '12.00-12.50').
rules.pass_condition: Stacked limits show MAX over MIN; inline limits show MIN-MAX.
rules.fail_condition: Stacked limits place MIN over MAX, or inline limits place MAX-MIN.
rules.remediation: Reorder stacked limits to MAX over MIN, or inline limits to MIN-MAX.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Metric Limits and Fits ISO Code Syntax (ANSI B4.2)
rules.audit_check: Where metric limits and fits symbols are used per ANSI B4.2, uppercase letters denote INTERNAL features (holes, e.g., H7) and lowercase letters denote EXTERNAL features (shafts, e.g., g6). Explicit numeric limit equivalents may be shown in parentheses for shop clarity.
rules.pass_condition: Internal features use uppercase ISO tolerance class letters (H, G, JS, etc.) and external features use lowercase letters (h, g, f, k, etc.).
rules.fail_condition: An external shaft is mistakenly called out with an uppercase hole class (e.g., Ø20H7 on a pin) or a hole with a lowercase shaft class (e.g., Ø20g6 on a bore).
rules.remediation: Use uppercase fit letters for internal holes/slots and lowercase fit letters for external shafts/tabs per ANSI B4.2.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Plus Value Above Minus Value for Unilateral and Bilateral Tolerances
rules.audit_check: For stacked unilateral and bilateral tolerances, the PLUS value SHALL be placed above the MINUS value.
rules.pass_condition: All stacked plus/minus tolerances display the '+' deviation on top and the '-' deviation on the bottom.
rules.fail_condition: A stacked tolerance places the minus value above the plus value.
rules.remediation: Place the plus tolerance value above the minus tolerance value.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Millimeter Tolerance Decimal Formatting (Unilateral Zero, Bilateral Match, Limit Match)
rules.audit_check: On millimeter drawings: (a) in unilateral tolerancing where one value is zero, a SINGLE zero '0' SHALL be shown WITHOUT a '+' or '-' sign (e.g., '+0.2 / 0', NOT '+0.2 / -0.0'); (b) in bilateral tolerancing, both '+' and '-' values SHALL have the same number of decimal places (nominal need not match); (c) in limit dimensioning, if either limit has decimals, the other SHALL add trailing zeros to match.
rules.pass_condition: Metric unilateral zeros are bare '0' without sign/decimals; bilateral pairs and limit pairs have matched decimal places.
rules.fail_condition: Metric unilateral tolerance displays '-0.00' or '+0'; bilateral '+' and '-' have mismatched decimal places (e.g., +0.2 / -0.05); or limit pair mismatches decimals (e.g., 12.5 / 12).
rules.remediation: Format metric unilateral zero as '0' (no sign), and pad bilateral/limit pairs to equal decimal places.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Inch Tolerance Decimal Formatting (Signed Matched Zero, Bilateral & Limit Match)
rules.audit_check: On decimal-inch drawings: (a) in unilateral tolerancing where one value is zero, it SHALL have the same number of decimal places as the nonzero value AND SHALL carry the opposite sign (e.g., '.500 +.005 / -.000'); (b) in bilateral tolerancing, nominal, '+', and '-' values SHALL all have the same number of decimal places; (c) in limit dimensioning, both limits SHALL match decimal places; (d) basic dimensions need not match FCF tolerance decimals.
rules.pass_condition: Inch unilateral zeros include opposite sign and matching decimal places (e.g., -.000); bilateral nominal/+/- and limit pairs all share identical decimal places.
rules.fail_condition: Inch unilateral zero omits sign or decimal places (e.g., '+.005 / 0'), or inch nominal/tolerance decimal counts disagree.
rules.remediation: Match decimal places across inch dimension and tolerance values and add the opposite sign to inch unilateral zero values.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Angular Tolerance Decimal Matching and Leading Zero < 1°
rules.audit_check: For angular tolerances, the angle and both plus/minus tolerance values SHALL have the same number of decimal places, and any angular tolerance value < 1° SHALL include a leading zero (e.g., '30.0° ±0.5°', even on inch drawings).
rules.pass_condition: Angular nominal and tolerance values have equal decimal places and sub-degree values include a leading zero (e.g., ±0.5°).
rules.fail_condition: Angular tolerance omits leading zero (e.g., '±.5°') or decimal places mismatch between angle and tolerance (e.g., '45° ±0.5°').
rules.remediation: Match decimal places on angle and tolerance (e.g., '45.0° ±0.5°') and always include leading zero for angles < 1°.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Absolute Limits (Infinite Trailing Zeros) & Plating/Coating Applicability (5.4.1)
rules.audit_check: All dimensional limits are absolute (interpreted as followed by infinite zeros). Where a part is to be plated or coated (5.4.1), the drawing or referenced document SHALL explicitly state whether dimensional limits apply BEFORE or AFTER plating/coating.
rules.pass_condition: Every drawing specifying plating, anodizing, painting, or coating explicitly notes 'DIMENSIONAL LIMITS APPLY AFTER [PROCESS]' or 'BEFORE [PROCESS]'.
rules.fail_condition: Drawing specifies plating/coating/anodizing in notes or title block without stating whether dimensions apply before or after coating.
rules.remediation: Add 'DIMENSIONAL LIMITS APPLY AFTER PLATING' (or BEFORE, substituting exact process name) to the general notes.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Single Limit Toleranced Dimensions (MIN / MAX Placement & Validity)
rules.audit_check: 'MIN' or 'MAX' SHALL be placed AFTER the dimension value, and may be used only where design intent is clear and the unspecified opposite limit approaching zero or infinity will not be detrimental to function.
rules.pass_condition: 'MIN'/'MAX' follows the dimension value and the unbounded direction is physically constrained or non-detrimental (e.g., corner radius R0.5 MAX, thread depth 15 MIN).
rules.fail_condition: 'MIN'/'MAX' precedes the dimension value, or is applied to a mating feature of size where an unbounded opposite limit would break assembly.
rules.remediation: Place 'MIN'/'MAX' after the dimension value, or replace with bilateral/limit tolerances if both bounds matter functionally.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Preferred Profile Tolerancing for Surface Location & Non-Datum Surface Accumulation
rules.audit_check: Profile tolerances with basic dimensions are the preferred practice for locating planar surfaces. Planar feature-to-feature relationships where neither surface is a referenced datum feature do NOT establish a direct requirement unless a feature-relating tolerance is applied.
rules.pass_condition: Planar surfaces are located via Profile of a Surface relative to a DRF, and critical surface-to-surface step distances either reference one surface as a datum or carry a dedicated feature-relating control.
rules.fail_condition: Critical step distance between two non-datum surfaces relies on indirect accumulation without a feature-relating profile or datum relationship.
rules.remediation: Reference one surface as a datum or apply a composite/feature-relating Profile tolerance between the surfaces.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Dimension Origin Symbol Does Not Establish a DRF or Control Origin Form
visual_syntax_triggers: Dimension Origin Symbol (○ on dimension line)
rules.audit_check: The Dimension Origin symbol designates which surface establishes the measurement origin plane, but (5.7 Note) it DOES NOT establish a Datum Reference Frame and does NOT control form of the origin surface.
rules.pass_condition: Origin surface has adequate form control (flatness/orientation) if functional, and is not mistakenly treated as a datum reference frame.
rules.fail_condition: Dimension origin symbol is used on an uncontrolled warped surface where angular/form variation would invalidate measurement, or treated as a substitute for a DRF.
rules.remediation: Add flatness/orientation control to the origin surface or replace with a formal Datum Feature + Profile/Orientation FCF.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Rule #1 (Envelope Principle): Perfect Form at MMC Default & LMC Inversion
rules.audit_check: UOS, Rule #1 governs every individual regular feature of size: (a) its surface SHALL NOT violate an envelope of perfect form at MMC; (b) form variation increases as local size departs toward LMC; (c) no perfect form at LMC exists by default; (d) EXCEPT when a geometric tolerance is applied at LMC, perfect form at LMC IS required and perfect form at MMC is removed; (e) non-opposed localized areas still may not violate LMC.
rules.pass_condition: Size tolerances on regular FOS align with Rule #1 envelope intent (and any intended override explicitly uses Ⓘ, Ⓕ, AVG, or FOS straightness/flatness per 5.8.2).
rules.fail_condition: Drawing adds a redundant surface form tolerance EQUAL TO or GREATER THAN the size tolerance on a regular FOS without invoking Ⓘ, Ⓕ, or AVG (violating Rule #1 hierarchy).
rules.remediation: Reduce surface form tolerance below the size tolerance, or invoke Ⓘ / Ⓕ / AVG / derived-median-line control if Rule #1 override is intended.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Rule #1 Exceptions & Independency Symbol (Ⓘ) Caution
rules.audit_check: Rule #1 does NOT apply to: (a) commercial stock surfaces left as-furnished, (b) tolerances with Free State Ⓕ, (c) Straightness/Flatness applied to a FOS (derived median line/plane), (d) features with the Independency symbol Ⓘ, or (e) Average Diameter (AVG). CAUTION (5.8.2(d)): Without a supplementary form control, feature form is COMPLETELY UNCONTROLLED wherever Ⓘ is applied.
rules.pass_condition: Every feature carrying Ⓘ is paired with an appropriate supplementary form/profile/orientation control (or uncontrolled form is functionally acceptable).
rules.fail_condition: Independency symbol Ⓘ is applied to a mating feature of size with NO supplementary form, orientation, or runout control.
rules.remediation: Add an explicit form tolerance (e.g., cylindricity, straightness, flatness) whenever Ⓘ is applied to a functional feature of size.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Limits of Size Do Not Control Orientation or Location Between Individual Features
rules.audit_check: Limits of size DO NOT control orientation or location between individual features. Features shown perpendicular, coaxial, or symmetrical SHALL be adequately toleranced for location/orientation. If perfect relationship at MMC is required, use (a) zero orientation at MMC, (b) zero position at MMC, or (c) an explicit 'PERFECT [ORIENTATION/COAXIALITY/LOCATION] AT MMC REQUIRED' note.
rules.pass_condition: All stepped coaxial diameters, perpendicular surfaces, and symmetrical tabs/slots have explicit geometric tolerances (Sections 9–12) controlling their interrelationship.
rules.fail_condition: Multiple stepped coaxial diameters or symmetrical features rely solely on size tolerances with no position, runout, orientation, or profile control relating them.
rules.remediation: Add Position, Runout, Orientation, or Profile FCFs (or zero tolerance at MMC) to relate the individual features.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Continuous Feature (CF) Required for Interrupted Coaxial/Coplanar Features of Size
rules.audit_check: The note 'CONTINUOUS FEATURE' or the 'CF' symbol SHALL be used to identify two or more interrupted features of size when they must be treated geometrically as a single feature of size (sharing one Rule #1 envelope). Connecting extension lines alone DO NOT establish a continuous feature (6.3.23).
rules.pass_condition: Interrupted coaxial/coplanar segments intended to act as a single feature carry the 'CF' symbol (or have an explicit coaxiality/coplanarity FCF).
rules.fail_condition: Two interrupted bosses/bores/pads are dimensioned once with connecting extension lines (without 'CF' and without a coaxiality/profile FCF), falsely assuming a single envelope.
rules.remediation: Add the 'CF' symbol adjacent to the size dimension or add a geometric tolerance relating the separate features.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Rule #2 (RFS/RMB Default) & Prohibition of MMC/LMC on Non-FOS Geometric Controls
rules.audit_check: RFS is the default for all geometric tolerance values and RMB is the default for all datum feature references (no RFS/RMB symbol exists in Y14.5-2018). PROHIBITED (5.9.1 Note): MMC (Ⓜ) and LMC (Ⓛ) SHALL NOT be applied to the tolerance value of Circular Runout, Total Runout, Orientation applied to a surface, Profile of a Line, Profile of a Surface, Circularity, or Cylindricity.
rules.pass_condition: Ⓜ and Ⓛ appear ONLY on tolerance values governing features of size (Position, FOS Orientation, Derived Median Line Straightness, Derived Median Plane Flatness) and on eligible datum feature references.
rules.fail_condition: Ⓜ or Ⓛ is placed inside the tolerance compartment of Profile, Runout, Circularity, Cylindricity, or surface-applied Flatness/Straightness/Orientation — OR an obsolete encircled 'S' (RFS) symbol appears.
rules.remediation: Remove Ⓜ/Ⓛ from the tolerance compartment of surface/runout/profile/roundness controls and remove any legacy Ⓢ (RFS) symbol.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Surface Method Precedence Over Axis Method for MMC/LMC Tolerances
rules.audit_check: When a geometric tolerance is applied at MMC or LMC and form deviations exist, the SURFACE method (Virtual Condition boundary non-violation) SHALL take precedence over the axis method. (Note 5.9.4.1 / 5.9.6.1: If MMC/LMC creates a negative Virtual Condition, the surface interpretation does not apply.)
rules.pass_condition: Tolerance stackups and inspection notes for Ⓜ/Ⓛ controls respect Virtual Condition boundary precedence (and do not yield invalid negative VCs where surface containment is intended).
rules.fail_condition: An MMC/LMC callout produces a mathematically negative Virtual Condition on a mating feature or drawing notes contradict surface-method precedence.
rules.remediation: Verify Virtual Condition calculations (MMC ± tol or LMC ± tol) and align inspection notes with surface-method precedence.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Screw Thread Pitch Cylinder Default & Exception Qualifier
rules.audit_check: UOS, every orientation/position tolerance and datum reference applied to a screw thread applies to the PITCH CYLINDER AXIS. Where an exception is required, the specific feature (e.g., 'MAJOR DIA' or 'MINOR DIA') SHALL be stated beneath or adjacent to the FCF or datum feature symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Thread FCFs and datums either intentionally reference the pitch cylinder axis or explicitly note 'MAJOR DIA' / 'MINOR DIA' beneath/adjacent to the symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Design functionally depends on thread major/minor diameter alignment without specifying 'MAJOR DIA' or 'MINOR DIA' adjacent to the FCF/datum.
rules.remediation: Add 'MAJOR DIA' or 'MINOR DIA' beneath or adjacent to the FCF/datum symbol if the pitch cylinder axis is not intended.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Mandatory Feature Designation for Gears and Splines (No Default)
visual_syntax_triggers: PITCH DIA / MAJOR DIA / MINOR DIA
rules.audit_check: Unlike screw threads, gears and splines have NO default axis feature: every orientation/position tolerance and datum reference applied to a gear or spline SHALL explicitly designate the specific feature (e.g., 'PITCH DIA', 'MAJOR DIA', 'MINOR DIA') beneath or adjacent to the FCF or datum feature symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Every FCF and datum feature symbol on a gear or spline explicitly specifies 'PITCH DIA', 'MAJOR DIA', or 'MINOR DIA'.
rules.fail_condition: An FCF or datum feature symbol is applied to a gear or spline without specifying which diameter (PITCH DIA, MAJOR DIA, or MINOR DIA) governs.
rules.remediation: Add 'PITCH DIA', 'MAJOR DIA', or 'MINOR DIA' immediately beneath or adjacent to the gear/spline FCF or datum symbol.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Directly Toleranced Angular Surface Creates Widening Wedge Zone (Prefer Angularity/Profile)
rules.audit_check: An angular surface defined by directly toleranced linear + angular dimensions produces a non-parallel widening tolerance zone. Where a uniform parallel tolerance zone is desired, Angularity or Profile tolerance SHOULD be used.
rules.pass_condition: Functional angled surfaces use a Basic angle + Angularity or Profile FCF for parallel tolerance boundaries.
rules.fail_condition: A precision mating angled surface relies on direct ± linear and ± angular tolerances causing uncontrolled wedge-zone widening.
rules.remediation: Replace direct ± angle tolerances on critical angled surfaces with a Basic angle and an Angularity or Profile FCF.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Conical Taper Specification Methods & Noncritical Taper Note
rules.audit_check: Precision conical tapers should be specified by (a) basic taper + basic diameter + profile, (b) size tolerance + profile, or (d) composite profile. Method (c) (toleranced diameters at both ends + toleranced length) is ONLY for noncritical transition tapers (5.14(c) Note).
rules.pass_condition: Critical/mating conical tapers use basic taper/diameter with Profile control or standard machine taper designation (ASME B5.10).
rules.fail_condition: A precision mating cone is toleranced solely by two independent ± end diameters and a ± length.
rules.remediation: Define critical tapers using a Basic taper/diameter with a Profile of a Surface (or composite Profile) FCF.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Flat Taper (Slope) Ratio Definition & Direct Radius Zone Interpretation (5.16.1)
rules.audit_check: Flat taper slope is defined as (H − h) / L (5.15). For a directly toleranced radius R (5.16.1), the surface must lie within two bounding arcs (concentric if the center is located; crescent-shaped tangent to adjacent surfaces if unlocated), and unlike CR, local flats/reversals ARE permitted within the zone.
rules.pass_condition: Flat taper ratios match (H − h)/L and standard 'R' is used only where local curvature reversals within the tolerance band are acceptable.
rules.fail_condition: Flat taper ratio conflicts with end heights/length, or 'R' is used on a high-stress fatigue fillet where sharp local kinks/reversals would cause failure (requiring CR).
rules.remediation: Verify slope ratio math and upgrade 'R' to 'CR' (with imperfection spec) or Profile if smooth curvature is fatigue-critical.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Controlled Radius (CR) — No Reversals & Recommended Imperfection Specification
rules.audit_check: A Controlled Radius (CR) requires a fair curve with NO flats or reversals and all local radii within limits.
