(5.16.2 Note): It is recommended that CR ONLY be used if its allowable imperfection limits are clarified by a general note, company/industry standard, or engineering specification referenced on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Every CR callout is backed by a referenced standard or general note defining allowable surface imperfection/inspection criteria.
rules.fail_condition: CR is specified on the drawing with no clarifying note or referenced standard defining allowable imperfection limits.
rules.remediation: Add a clarifying note/standard reference for CR inspection limits, or use standard 'R' if a fair-curve restriction is not functionally required.

rules.section: Section 5: Tolerancing, Interpretation of Limits, Limits of Size, and Material Condition Modifiers
rules.title: Statistical Tolerancing Symbol (<ST>) Mandatory Note & SPC Indices Caution
rules.audit_check: Whenever the Statistical Tolerancing symbol ⟨ST⟩ is used, a note SHALL be placed on the drawing stating: (a) 'FEATURES IDENTIFIED WITH THE STATISTICALLY TOLERANCED SYMBOL SHALL BE PRODUCED WITH STATISTICAL PROCESS CONTROLS' (or (b) '...OR TO THE MORE RESTRICTIVE ARITHMETIC LIMITS' if dual limits are shown). CAUTION: Necessary statistical indices (e.g., Cpk/Ppk) SHOULD also be specified.
rules.pass_condition: Every drawing using ⟨ST⟩ includes the mandatory SPC note and specifies required capability indices (e.g., Cpk ≥ 1.33).
rules.fail_condition: ⟨ST⟩ appears on dimensions or FCFs without the mandatory SPC general note (or omits capability indices).
rules.remediation: Add the mandatory 5.18(a)/(b) SPC note and specify required statistical capability indices (e.g., Cpk).

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Symbol Clarity and Legibility per ASME Y14.2
rules.audit_check: All GD&T and dimensioning symbols SHALL conform to ASME Y14.5-2018 proportions (Nonmandatory Appendix C) and meet legibility/reproducibility requirements of ASME Y14.2.
rules.pass_condition: All symbols are crisp, standard-compliant, and unobstructed.
rules.fail_condition: Non-standard, distorted, corrupted font characters, or illegible symbols appear in callouts or FCFs.
rules.remediation: Replace non-standard or corrupted glyphs with standard ASME Y14.5-2018 / Y14.2 symbols.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Datum Feature Symbol — Forbidden Letters (I, O, Q), Uniqueness, and Prohibition on Center Lines/Axes
rules.audit_check: Datum feature symbols SHALL use uppercase alphabet letters EXCEPT 'I', 'O', and 'Q' (which are PROHIBITED). Each distinct datum feature SHALL receive a unique letter (using double letters AA–AZ, BA–BZ in a rectangular frame only after exhausting single letters). PROHIBITED: The datum feature symbol SHALL NOT be applied to center lines, center planes, or axes.
rules.pass_condition: All datum letters exclude I, O, and Q; every unique datum feature has a unique letter; no datum triangle attaches directly to a center line, center plane, or axis.
rules.fail_condition: Datum letter I, O, or Q is used; two different datum features share the same letter; legacy boxed '-A-' style is used; or a datum triangle sits on a center line/axis.
rules.remediation: Rename forbidden/duplicate datum letters and attach the datum triangle to the surface outline, extension line, size dimension line, or FCF per 6.3.2.1/6.3.2.2.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Valid Datum Feature Triangle Attachment Locations (Surface vs. Feature of Size)
rules.audit_check: When a datum is a PLANAR SURFACE, the datum triangle on an extension line SHALL be clearly separated from the dimension line (6.3.2.1(b)). When a datum is an AXIS OR CENTER PLANE of a FOS, the datum triangle is placed in-line with the size dimension line (6.3.2.1(d)), on the horizontal leader of a hole size dimension (f), attached to an FCF governing the FOS (g), or on a cylindrical outline separated from size (e).
rules.pass_condition: Datum triangle placement unambiguously distinguishes planar surface datums from FOS axis/center-plane datums.
rules.fail_condition: A datum triangle intended for a planar surface is accidentally aligned with a size dimension line (making it a center plane), OR a width FOS datum triangle is misaligned from the size dimension line (making it only one face).
rules.remediation: Align the datum triangle directly with the size dimension line/FCF for a FOS datum, or offset it clearly away from the dimension line for a single surface datum.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Datum Target Symbol Construction, Sequential Numbering, and Dashed Far-Side Leaders
rules.audit_check: A Datum Target symbol SHALL be a horizontally divided circle with datum letter + sequential target number starting at 1 (e.g., A1, A2, A3) in the lower half, and area size (if area target) in the upper half. It SHOULD sit outside the part outline. In 2D views, a SOLID radial leader indicates the near (visible) surface and a DASHED radial leader indicates the far (hidden) surface. In 3D models, the leader is always solid. When combined with a datum feature symbol, associated target numbers separated by commas (e.g., A1, A2, A3) SHALL appear near the datum feature symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Target circles are properly split, numbered sequentially from 1, use solid/dashed leaders accurately for near/far faces, and list target IDs near any paired datum feature symbol.
rules.fail_condition: Target numbering skips/duplicates numbers or does not start at 1, solid leader points to a hidden far surface in 2D, or paired datum feature symbol omits target IDs.
rules.remediation: Correct datum target circle formatting, sequential numbering, and solid/dashed leader style.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Datum Target Point (X), Line (Phantom/X), and Area (Section-Lined Phantom) Symbols
rules.audit_check: Target points (6.3.3.2) SHALL use an 'X' symbol located in a direct view (or two adjacent views if no direct view exists). Target lines (6.3.3.3) SHALL use an 'X' on the edge view, a phantom line on the direct view, or both. Target areas (6.3.3.4) SHALL use section-lined hatching inside a phantom outline in 2D (supplemental geometry in 3D), with size/shape specified in the upper circle half, by basic dimensions, or by a dot-terminated leader into the upper half.
rules.pass_condition: Every datum target point, line, and area uses the correct graphical symbology and has complete location/size definition.
rules.fail_condition: Target point is located in only one non-direct view, target area lacks size/shape specification, or non-standard hatching/lines are used.
rules.remediation: Add direct-view (or two-view) location dimensions for target points/lines and specify exact size/shape for target areas.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Basic Dimension Rectangle & Prefix Symbols Without Spaces (6.3.7, 6.3.12–6.3.16)
rules.audit_check: Basic dimensions SHALL be enclosed in a rectangle (unless governed by an 'UNTOLERANCED DIMENSIONS ARE BASIC' note). The symbols Ø, SØ, R, SR, CR (6.3.7), Counterbore ⌴ (6.3.12), Spotface (6.3.13), Countersink ⌵ (6.3.14), Depth ↧ (6.3.15), and Square □ (6.3.16) SHALL PRECEDE their numeric value with NO SPACE between symbol and value.
rules.pass_condition: All prefix symbols directly precede their numerals with zero space (e.g., Ø10, ⌴Ø16, ↧8, □20).
rules.fail_condition: A space separates symbol and value (e.g., 'Ø 10', '↧ 8'), or symbol is placed after the value.
rules.remediation: Place prefix symbols immediately before the dimension value with no intervening space.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Reference Symbol Parentheses on Graphics vs. 'REFERENCE'/'REF' in Written Notes
rules.audit_check: Reference dimensions/data on drawing graphics SHALL be enclosed in parentheses '(...)'. However, inside written notes, parentheses retain grammatical meaning UOS, so reference data inside written notes SHALL use 'REFERENCE' or 'REF'.
rules.pass_condition: Graphic reference dimensions use parentheses '(...)' and reference values inside prose notes use 'REF' or 'REFERENCE'.
rules.fail_condition: Prose note encloses a reference value solely in parentheses expecting reference-dimension interpretation, or graphic dimension uses 'REF' instead of parentheses.
rules.remediation: Use '(...)' on graphic dimensions and 'REF'/'REFERENCE' inside written notes.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Arc Length Symbol Placement Above Dimension & Taper/Slope Orientation (6.3.18)
rules.audit_check: The Arc Length symbol SHALL be placed ABOVE the dimension (not preceding it) and applies to the nearest surface (6.3.9). Conical Taper and Flat Slope symbols SHALL always be oriented with their vertical leg to the LEFT (6.3.18).
rules.pass_condition: Arc length symbol sits above the value; taper/slope symbols show vertical leg on the left.
rules.fail_condition: Arc length symbol precedes the value instead of sitting above it, or a taper/slope symbol is mirrored with vertical leg on the right.
rules.remediation: Place arc length symbol above the numeral and orient taper/slope symbols with vertical leg to the left.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Modifier Ordering Inside Feature Control Frames (6.3.10, 6.3.20–6.3.22, 6.4.1, 6.4.7)
rules.audit_check: Inside the tolerance compartment of an FCF: (1) Ø or SØ (if applicable) SHALL precede the tolerance value; (2) material condition modifier (Ⓜ/Ⓛ) follows the tolerance value; (3) additional modifiers follow in proper position — Ⓤ followed by material-added value (6.3.22), Ⓣ (6.3.21), Ⓟ + minimum height (6.4.7), Ⓕ (6.3.20), ⟨ST⟩ (6.3.10), or Δ (6.3.31). When Ⓕ applies to a datum reference, it follows the datum letter and any MMB/LMB modifier (6.3.20).
rules.pass_condition: All tolerance and datum modifiers appear in valid compartments and legal sequence per Section 6.3/6.4.
rules.fail_condition: Ø follows the tolerance value, modifiers are placed before the tolerance value, Ⓤ omits its second numeric value, or Ⓕ precedes Ⓜ/Ⓛ.
rules.remediation: Reorder FCF compartment entries to: [Symbol] | [Ø/SØ][Value][Ⓜ/Ⓛ][Ⓟ/Ⓣ/Ⓤ value/Δ/Ⓕ/⟨ST⟩] | [Datum][Ⓜ/Ⓛ][Ⓕ][▷][DOF] | ...

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: All Around (○), All Over (◎○), Between (↔), and From-To (→) Symbols (6.3.11, 6.3.25, 6.3.32)
rules.audit_check: The 'All Around' circle SHALL sit at the junction (elbow) of the FCF leader and applies only to the view shown (never in a 2D axonometric view per 11.3.1.3). 'All Over' applies to the full 3D surface. 'Between' (G ↔ H) and 'From-To' (A → B) SHALL direct the FCF leader to the actual portion of the feature being controlled, with extremity letters clearly labeled on the view.
rules.pass_condition: All Around/All Over circles sit cleanly on the leader elbow; Between/From-To extremity labels exist on the view and the leader touches the governed segment.
rules.fail_condition: All Around circle appears in an isometric/axonometric 2D view, extremity letters referenced in 'G ↔ H' or 'A → B' are missing from the drawing, or leader points to the wrong segment.
rules.remediation: Move All Around to an orthographic view (or use All Over), and verify all extremity labels and leader landing segments.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Continuous Feature ('CF') Placement & Extension Lines Not Sufficient Alone
rules.audit_check: The 'CF' symbol SHALL be placed adjacent to the size dimension of an interrupted regular FOS, adjacent to a geometric tolerance for an interrupted surface, or adjacent to a datum feature symbol applied to interrupted features. Extension lines connecting separated surfaces BY THEMSELVES DO NOT establish a continuous feature. 'n SURFACES' may be added beside 'CF' for clarity.
rules.pass_condition: 'CF' is explicitly placed on interrupted features intended to share a single geometric/size boundary, with optional 'n SURFACES' where helpful.
rules.fail_condition: Drawing relies solely on bridging extension lines across interrupted pads/bosses without 'CF' or a coplanarity/position FCF.
rules.remediation: Add 'CF' (and 'n SURFACES' if helpful) adjacent to the governing size dimension, FCF, or datum feature symbol.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Movable Datum Target Symbol Triangle Alignment
rules.audit_check: The Movable Datum Target triangular pointer is aligned with the horizontal dividing line of the datum target circle (pointing left or right) with the leader extending from the tip of the triangle; triangle orientation does NOT denote movement direction.
rules.pass_condition: Movable datum target pointer attaches aligned to the circle's horizontal divider with leader from its tip (and direction of motion defined per 7.24.2 if non-normal).
rules.fail_condition: Pointer is misattached, or movement direction is left undefined when non-normal to the true profile.
rules.remediation: Align the movable target triangle with the target circle midline and specify movement direction per 7.24.2 when non-normal.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Datum Reference Frame Symbol Construction (X, Y, Z Axis Labels)
rules.audit_check: Where a Datum Reference Frame symbol is shown on the drawing or model, it SHALL consist of the uppercase X, Y, and Z coordinate labels applied to the mutually perpendicular axes of the datum reference frame.
rules.pass_condition: Displayed DRF symbol includes right-handed mutually perpendicular axes labeled X, Y, and Z.
rules.fail_condition: DRF symbol omits one or more axis labels or uses non-standard axis identifiers without explanation.
rules.remediation: Label all three mutually perpendicular axes of the DRF symbol with uppercase X, Y, and Z.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Feature Control Frame Mandatory Structure (1 of 12 Valid Symbols + Tolerance)
rules.audit_check: Every Feature Control Frame SHALL be a compartmented rectangle containing: (1) exactly 1 of the 12 valid ASME Y14.5-2018 geometric characteristic symbols (Straightness, Flatness, Circularity, Cylindricity, Profile of a Line, Profile of a Surface, Angularity, Perpendicularity, Parallelism, Position, Circular Runout, Total Runout); (2) a tolerance value (or 'NONUNIFORM' / 'TOL <letter>'); and (3) datum feature references in separate compartments left-to-right in order of precedence where applicable (6.4.2, 6.4.3).
rules.pass_condition: Every FCF has valid compartments, one of the 12 legal symbols, a valid tolerance value, and properly separated datum compartments.
rules.fail_condition: FCF uses an invalid/deprecated symbol, omits a tolerance value, combines non-common datums without vertical dividers, or puts a datum reference in a Form FCF.
rules.remediation: Correct the FCF compartment structure to conform to 6.4.1–6.4.3.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Composite FCF Restricted Strictly to Position and Profile Symbols
rules.audit_check: A Composite Feature Control Frame (one geometric symbol spanning two or more stacked segments) is permitted ONLY for POSITION (⌖) or PROFILE (⌓/⌒) — plus stacked unit-basis Straightness/Flatness per 8.4.1.4/8.4.2.2. Composite FCFs SHALL NOT be used for Orientation, Runout, Circularity, or Cylindricity.
rules.pass_condition: Composite FCFs contain only Position or Profile (or valid unit-basis Straightness/Flatness) with decreasing tolerance values in lower segments.
rules.fail_condition: A composite FCF spans Perpendicularity, Parallelism, Angularity, or Runout, or has a lower-segment tolerance >= the upper-segment tolerance.
rules.remediation: Replace illegal composite frames with multiple single-segment FCFs (6.4.5) and ensure lower-segment tolerances are strictly smaller than upper segments.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Multiple Single-Segment FCFs Repeat Symbol in Every Row & Combined FCF + Datum Symbol (6.4.6)
visual_syntax_triggers: Datum Feature Symbol Attached to FCF
rules.audit_check: Multiple single-segment FCFs (6.4.5) SHALL show an individual geometric characteristic symbol in EACH horizontal segment (distinguishing them from composite FCFs). When a controlled feature also serves as a datum feature (6.4.6), the datum feature symbol may attach directly above or below the FCF (applying to the feature/pattern controlled by that FCF).
rules.pass_condition: Multiple single-segment FCFs repeat the characteristic symbol in each row; attached datum symbols unambiguously identify the controlled feature(s).
rules.fail_condition: A stacked multi-segment FCF omits the geometric symbol on a lower row while attempting to change datum precedence/DRF (creating an illegal composite FCF).
rules.remediation: Include the geometric symbol in each row of multiple single-segment FCFs whenever lower segments constrain translation or alter the DRF.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Projected Tolerance Zone (Ⓟ) Minimum Height Required in FCF or View Chain Line
rules.audit_check: When Ⓟ is specified in a Position or Orientation FCF, the minimum projection height SHALL immediately follow Ⓟ inside the FCF — UNLESS in 2D orthographic views the projection direction/height is clarified with a dimensioned chain line, in which case the height value may be omitted from the FCF.
rules.pass_condition: Ⓟ is followed by a numeric minimum projection height in the FCF, or a dimensioned chain line clearly shows both direction and minimum projection height in the view.
rules.fail_condition: Ⓟ appears in the FCF with NO height value AND NO dimensioned chain line in the view, or projection direction on a through-hole is ambiguous.
rules.remediation: Add the minimum projection height immediately after Ⓟ in the FCF and add a chain line whenever projection direction could be ambiguous.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Valid Feature Control Frame Placement Methods
rules.audit_check: Every FCF SHALL be associated with its considered feature via one of the six valid methods: (a) below/beside a leader-directed note/dimension, (b) leader from FCF to feature/extension line, (c) side/corner/end attached to extension line, (d) side/corner/end attached to extension of a FOS dimension line, (e) in a note/chart/general tolerance block, or (f) attached to another properly placed FCF.
rules.pass_condition: Every FCF connects unambiguously to its controlled feature(s) via methods (a)–(f).
rules.fail_condition: An FCF floats disconnected on the drawing without a leader, note reference, or attachment, or attaches ambiguously between two unrelated dimensions.
rules.remediation: Attach the FCF clearly using one of methods 6.5(a)–(f).

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Diameter/Spherical Diameter Symbol Mandatory for Cylindrical/Spherical Zones & Prohibited for Width/Planar Zones
rules.audit_check: When a tolerance zone is cylindrical or spherical (e.g., round hole/pin position, cylindrical axis perpendicularity, derived median line straightness), Ø or SØ SHALL precede the tolerance value. When the zone is planar/width/profile/runout (e.g., flat surface, slot center plane, bidirectional hole position), Ø and SØ SHALL BE OMITTED.
rules.pass_condition: Ø/SØ precedes cylindrical/spherical tolerance zones and is omitted on all planar, width, profile, circularity, cylindricity, and runout zones.
rules.fail_condition: A round-hole Position FCF omits Ø (without bidirectional intent), OR Ø is erroneously placed in a Flatness, Profile, Runout, Slot-width Position, or Planar-surface Orientation FCF.
rules.remediation: Add Ø/SØ for cylindrical/spherical axis/point zones; remove Ø/SØ from all planar, width, profile, circularity, cylindricity, and runout FCFs.

rules.section: Section 6: Symbology and Feature Control Frame Construction
rules.title: Tabulated Tolerance Syntax ('TOL <Letter>')
rules.audit_check: When the tolerance value in an FCF is tabulated, a letter preceded by the abbreviation 'TOL' (e.g., 'TOL A') SHALL be entered in the tolerance compartment, and the corresponding table SHALL define the values for that letter.
rules.pass_condition: Tabulated FCF displays 'TOL <letter>' and a matching column/row exists in the drawing table.
rules.fail_condition: FCF uses a bare letter without 'TOL', or references a 'TOL <letter>' missing from the table.
rules.remediation: Format the tolerance compartment as 'TOL <letter>' and verify the matching entry in the drawing table.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Primary Datum Feature DOF Constraint Audit (Avoiding Redundant/Over-Constrained Datums)
rules.audit_check: Audit the 6 DOFs constrained by primary datum features RMB: planar surface = 3 DOFs (1T, 2R); width = 3 DOFs (1T, 2R); sphere = 3 DOFs (3T); cylinder = 4 DOFs (2T, 2R); cone = 5 DOFs (3T, 2R); linear extruded shape = 5 DOFs (2T, 3R); complex surface = 6 DOFs (3T, 3R). Adding secondary/tertiary datums after all 6 DOFs are already constrained by higher-precedence RMB datums is redundant (unless a customized DRF per 7.22 or MMB/LMB datum shift is used).
rules.pass_condition: Each secondary and tertiary datum feature in an FCF constrains at least one remaining unconstrained DOF (or intentionally operates under MMB/LMB shift or customized DRF).
rules.fail_condition: A tertiary datum is referenced after a primary plane (3 DOF) + secondary RMB cylinder (2T) + tertiary parallel plane (already constrained), OR a secondary/tertiary datum follows a 6-DOF complex primary RMB datum with zero remaining DOFs.
rules.remediation: Remove redundant datum references that constrain zero remaining DOFs, or use a Customized DRF (7.22) if partial DOF release is intended.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: True Geometric Counterpart Inverse Shape & Fixed/Adjustable Requirements (7.5.2)
rules.audit_check: UOS, a true geometric counterpart is the perfect-form inverse shape of the datum feature, basically oriented and basically located to other counterparts in the FCF (unless ▷ or movable datum target unlocks location), fixed at designated size for MMB/LMB, and adjustable in size for RMB.
rules.pass_condition: All datum features referenced in a DRF have well-defined basic angular/locational relationships (or explicit ▷/movable targets) enabling true geometric counterpart construction.
rules.fail_condition: Two datum features referenced in the same FCF lack a basic dimension (or implied 90°/0° basic relationship) relating their mutual orientation or location.
rules.remediation: Ensure basic dimensions (or implied 0°/90° basic relationships) connect all datum features referenced in the same DRF.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Distinct Datum Precedence or Modifiers Create Distinct Datum Reference Frames
rules.audit_check: Each FCF SHALL contain all applicable datum feature references. Any difference in datum letters, order of precedence (e.g., |A|B|C| vs |A|C|B|), or material boundary modifiers (e.g., |A|BⓂ| vs |A|B|) establishes a DIFFERENT Datum Reference Frame.
rules.pass_condition: Consistent DRFs are referenced across functionally simultaneous features, and where multiple DRFs exist, their relationship is explicitly controlled per 7.14.
rules.fail_condition: Features intended to share one DRF accidentally swap datum order or omit/add a boundary modifier inconsistently, or two separate DRFs have no tolerance relating them (7.14).
rules.remediation: Unify datum order and modifiers where one DRF is intended, or specify geometric tolerances relating multiple DRFs per 7.14.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Datum Features Shall Be Readily Discernible, Accessible, and Functional
rules.audit_check: Datum features SHALL be readily discernible on the produced part (on symmetrical parts or identical features, physical identification may be needed). Datum features SHOULD be functional mating features, accessible, of sufficient size, and permanent surfaces not removed by later machining (7.8.1).
rules.pass_condition: Every identified datum feature is physically identifiable, accessible, large enough for repeatable orientation/location, and matches assembly function.
rules.fail_condition: A tiny chamfer, short/unstable secondary face, or ambiguous feature on an otherwise symmetric part is chosen as a primary datum without physical identification.
rules.remediation: Select accessible, functionally mating, stable features as datums, or add an asymmetric/marked identification feature on symmetric parts.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Mandatory Geometric & Size Controls on Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Datum Features
rules.audit_check: Datum features SHALL be controlled by appropriate geometric tolerances and/or size dimensions, AND a geometric relationship between datum features in a DRF SHALL be specified so true geometric counterpart boundaries can be calculated: (a) Primary datum feature: size and form (e.g., flatness/cylindricity) and/or pattern inter-location; (b) Secondary datum feature: size, orientation, and/or location relative to Primary; (c) Tertiary datum feature: size, orientation, and/or location relative to Primary and Secondary.
rules.pass_condition: Primary datum has form control (or FOS size + form), Secondary datum is oriented/located to Primary, and Tertiary datum is oriented/located to Primary and Secondary.
rules.fail_condition: A planar primary datum lacks flatness/profile form control, OR a secondary/tertiary datum feature has NO geometric tolerance (perpendicularity, position, profile, etc.) relating it back to higher-precedence datums (making MMB/LMB/OB impossible to calculate).
rules.remediation: Apply flatness/form control to primary planar datums and orientation/position/profile tolerances relating secondary and tertiary datums to higher-precedence datums.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Datum Features Listed Left-to-Right in Order of Precedence & No Duplicate/Undefined Datums
rules.audit_check: Datum feature references SHALL be entered left-to-right in desired order of precedence (primary, secondary, tertiary) to constrain required DOFs. Every datum letter referenced in an FCF SHALL exist as a defined Datum Feature Symbol or Datum Target set on the drawing (and no datum feature shall reference itself illegally or repeat the same single datum twice in one FCF).
rules.pass_condition: Every datum letter in every FCF maps to an existing datum feature/target on the drawing, is ordered functionally left-to-right, and constrains required DOFs without redundant repetition.
rules.fail_condition: An FCF references a datum letter (e.g., 'D') that is never defined anywhere on the drawing, duplicates the same datum letter in one FCF (e.g., |A|B|A|), or references a datum to itself (e.g., Perpendicularity of A to A).
rules.remediation: Define missing datum feature symbols, remove duplicate/self-referential datum references, and order datums functionally left-to-right.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Rocking / Unstable Datum Feature Default Stabilization
rules.audit_check: Where irregularities on an RMB datum feature cause the part to rock/become unstable on its true geometric counterpart, the default is a single solution minimizing separation per ASME Y14.5.1M. If another fitting routine (e.g., least squares, Chebychev, candidate datum set) is required, it SHALL be explicitly specified on the drawing.
rules.pass_condition: Default minimum-separation stabilization applies, or an explicit fitting-method note (or datum targets) is specified on the drawing.
rules.fail_condition: A convex/cast/rough surface prone to rocking is used as a full-plane datum without datum targets, tight flatness, or a specified stabilization note.
rules.remediation: Control primary datum flatness tightly, use 3 datum targets, or state the required mathematical fitting method.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Prohibition of MMB (Ⓜ) or LMB (Ⓛ) on a Primary Planar Datum Feature
rules.audit_check: RMB is implied when no modifier is shown on a datum feature reference. MMB (Ⓜ) or LMB (Ⓛ) modifiers may be applied to datum feature references EXCEPT WHERE THE PRIMARY DATUM FEATURE IS PLANAR (a primary planar datum has no boundary size/location relative to higher datums, so Ⓜ/Ⓛ is strictly invalid on it).
rules.pass_condition: Primary planar datum references carry NO Ⓜ or Ⓛ modifier (they apply RMB only).
rules.fail_condition: A planar surface acting as the PRIMARY datum feature is referenced with Ⓜ or Ⓛ in the first datum compartment (e.g., |⌖|Ø0.2Ⓜ|AⓂ|B|C| where A is a flat plane).
rules.remediation: Remove Ⓜ or Ⓛ from any primary planar datum feature reference.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Complex Primary Datum Feature RMB vs. [BSC] or Datum Targets
rules.audit_check: Referencing a complex contoured surface as primary RMB can create a difficult variable-scale simulation requirement. For complex primary datums, specify datum targets, '[BSC]' (basic fixed counterpart), or an explicit stabilization/fitting method.
rules.pass_condition: Complex contoured primary datums use datum targets, '[BSC]', or an explicit mathematical fitting routine.
rules.fail_condition: A complex freeform sculpted surface is referenced primary RMB with no datum targets, no '[BSC]', and no math fitting method.
rules.remediation: Add datum targets, append '[BSC]' to the datum reference, or specify the mathematical fitting routine.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Datum Precedence Respected in MMB/LMB/RMB Boundary Calculations (7.11.6, 7.11.8, 7.11.9)
rules.audit_check: When calculating the true geometric counterpart size at MMB (7.11.6) or LMB (7.11.8), datum feature precedence SHALL be respected (except customized DRFs). If an MMB strictly equal to MMC (or LMB equal to LMC) is required for a secondary/tertiary datum feature, a ZERO geometric tolerance at MMC (or LMC) relative to higher-precedence datums must be applied to that datum feature (or an explicit bracketed simulator size specified per 7.11.10).
rules.pass_condition: Every datum feature referenced at Ⓜ or Ⓛ has well-defined tolerances relative to higher-precedence datums yielding a deterministic MMB/LMB (or explicit '[value]' size).
rules.fail_condition: A datum feature is referenced at Ⓜ or Ⓛ without the size or geometric controls needed to compute its MMB/LMB relative to higher-precedence datums.
rules.remediation: Apply the governing size and geometric tolerance (or zero tol at MMC/LMC, or explicit '[Øvalue]') to the datum feature.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Explicit Fixed-Size Simulator Boundary '[value]' / '[BSC]' Prohibits MMB/LMB Modifiers
rules.audit_check: Where an explicit fixed-size true geometric counterpart is specified, the value (preceded by Ø, R, SØ, or SR as applicable) or '[BSC]' SHALL be enclosed in square brackets following the datum letter and any free-state modifier. RMB, MMB (Ⓜ), and LMB (Ⓛ) are NOT APPLICABLE and SHALL NOT be combined with a bracketed explicit simulator size.
rules.pass_condition: Explicit simulator boundaries use square brackets (e.g., '|B[Ø10.2]|' or '|B[BSC]|') without Ⓜ or Ⓛ.
rules.fail_condition: A datum compartment combines Ⓜ or Ⓛ with an explicit bracketed size (e.g., '|BⓂ[Ø10.2]|') or omits Ø/R inside the brackets for a cylindrical/radius simulator.
rules.remediation: Remove Ⓜ/Ⓛ when specifying an explicit bracketed simulator size '[Ø...]' or '[BSC]'.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Datum Feature Shift (MMB/LMB) Moves Pattern as a Group Only & Must Remain Within MMB-LMB
rules.audit_check: MMB or LMB on a datum reference permits the pattern of controlled features to shift/rotate AS A GROUP (it NEVER adds individual feature-to-feature bonus tolerance per 10.3.6.2(a)). Where a datum feature can rotate away from a fixed counterpart (e.g., offset planar datum at MMB), at least one extremity of the datum feature SHALL remain between MMB and LMB.
rules.pass_condition: Datum shift at Ⓜ/Ⓛ aligns with functional mating clearance (assembly shift of the entire pattern as a rigid group).
rules.fail_condition: MMB/LMB datum modifier is applied on a precision locating/timing datum where rigid-body shift of the controlled pattern would break mating function (e.g., gear centers or optical alignment).
rules.remediation: Remove Ⓜ/Ⓛ from the datum reference (reverting to RMB) if datum shift of the pattern is functionally unacceptable.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Datum Translation Modifier (▷) Placement and Unlocking Behavior
rules.audit_check: When a true geometric counterpart's basic location must be unlocked to translate while maintaining orientation to higher-precedence datums, the Translation Modifier (▷) SHALL follow the datum feature reference and any other applicable modifiers (e.g., '|BⓂ▷|' or '|B▷|').
rules.pass_condition: ▷ appears only on secondary/tertiary datum references where unlocking translation is intended, placed after the datum letter and any MMB/LMB/Free-State modifier.
rules.fail_condition: ▷ is placed on a primary datum (meaningless/redundant) or placed before Ⓜ/Ⓛ.
rules.remediation: Place ▷ after the datum letter and any material boundary/free-state modifier on secondary/tertiary datums only.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Common Datum Features Syntax (Dash-Separated in One Compartment + Modifier on EACH Letter)
rules.audit_check: When two or more datum features establish a single common datum, their letters SHALL be separated by a dash inside ONE FCF compartment (e.g., '|A-B|'). Where MMB or LMB is required, the modifier SHALL follow EACH datum feature letter individually (e.g., '|AⓂ-BⓂ|', NOT '|A-BⓂ|'). For runout tolerances (7.12.2), common datum features can ONLY apply RMB (no Ⓜ/Ⓛ).
rules.pass_condition: Common datums appear in one compartment separated by a hyphen, with individual modifiers on every applicable letter (and RMB only for runout).
rules.fail_condition: Modifier is applied only to the trailing letter when both features require MMB/LMB (e.g., '|A-BⓂ|' unintentionally leaving A at RMB), or Ⓜ/Ⓛ is placed on common datums in a Runout FCF.
rules.remediation: Apply Ⓜ or Ⓛ after each applicable datum letter in the common datum compartment (or remove Ⓜ/Ⓛ completely for runout).

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Pattern of Features of Size Used as a Single Datum Feature (MMB vs. RMB 7.12.4)
visual_syntax_triggers: Datum Feature Triangle on Hole Pattern
rules.audit_check: When a pattern of features of size (e.g., '4X Ø10') serves as a single datum feature, the pattern SHALL have basic inter-feature dimensions and a positional (or geometric) tolerance establishing its true geometric counterpart boundary (7.9, 7.12.3), and the datum feature symbol SHALL attach to the pattern callout/FCF (not ambiguously to one hole alone unless only one hole is the datum).
rules.pass_condition: Pattern-as-datum has basic inter-hole dimensions, a controlling Position FCF, and unambiguous datum symbol attachment to the 'nX' pattern callout.
rules.fail_condition: A datum triangle is placed on an 'nX' hole pattern without inter-feature basic dimensions or without a controlling FCF defining the pattern's MMB/RMB simulator.
rules.remediation: Dimension pattern spacing with Basic dimensions, add a Position FCF to the datum pattern, and attach the datum symbol directly to the pattern FCF.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Partial Surface Datum Feature Indication (Chain Line + Dimensions)
visual_syntax_triggers: Datum Feature Triangle on Chain Line
rules.audit_check: Where only part of a surface serves as a datum feature, in 2D orthographic views a chain line drawn parallel to the surface profile SHALL be dimensioned to define area and location (with the datum feature triangle placed on the chain line per 6.3.2.1(h)); in 3D models supplemental geometry defines the partial surface.
rules.pass_condition: Partial datum chain line is drawn parallel to the surface, clearly dimensioned for extent and location, and carries the datum feature symbol.
rules.fail_condition: A chain line with a datum symbol lacks dimensions defining its start/end/length (where boundaries are not self-evident).
rules.remediation: Dimension the length and location of the partial datum chain line.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Mathematically Defined Contoured Datum Surface Requirement
rules.audit_check: Where a compound curve or contoured surface is used as a datum feature, it SHALL be mathematically defined in a 3D coordinate system (e.g., via CAD dataset or equation), and additional datum features are required if it does not constrain all necessary DOFs.
rules.pass_condition: Contoured datum surface references a defined 3D mathematical model/equation in a labeled coordinate system.
rules.fail_condition: A contoured spline/freeform surface is identified as a datum feature with no mathematical definition or referenced CAD data.
rules.remediation: Reference the authoritative 3D mathematical CAD data and coordinate system for contoured datum features.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Relationship Between Multiple Datum Reference Frames Shall Be Specified
visual_syntax_triggers: Multiple Datum Reference Frames (e.g., A|B|C and D|E|F)
rules.audit_check: When more than one DRF exists on a part and it is necessary to determine relationships and calculate boundaries between them, the geometric relationship between the DRFs SHALL be specified by tolerances linking their datum features.
rules.pass_condition: All separate DRFs on a part are tied together through explicit geometric tolerances relating their respective datum features.
rules.fail_condition: Two or more DRFs (e.g., [A,B,C] and [D,E,F]) exist on one part with no geometric tolerance controlling D, E, or F relative to A, B, and C.
rules.remediation: Add geometric tolerances controlling the datum features of secondary DRFs relative to the primary DRF.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Rotational Constraint About a Datum Axis or Point
rules.audit_check: Whenever the angular orientation (clocking) of a feature or pattern around a datum axis matters functionally (7.10.4, 7.16), a lower-precedence datum feature (e.g., keyway, slot, flat, offset pin/hole) SHALL be referenced in the FCF to constrain rotation about that axis.
rules.pass_condition: Clocking-sensitive features around a cylindrical datum include a tertiary (or secondary) anti-rotation datum feature in the FCF.
rules.fail_condition: A non-axisymmetric hole pattern or keyed feature located by basic X/Y coordinates from a cylindrical datum references ONLY '|A|B|' (plane + cylinder) with no clocking datum, leaving rotation completely unconstrained.
rules.remediation: Add a clocking datum feature (flat, slot, keyway, or secondary hole) as the tertiary datum reference in the FCF.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Irregular Features of Size as Datums — RMB Fitting Complexity Caution
rules.audit_check: Irregular features of size may serve as datums at MMB, LMB, or RMB. However (7.17(b) Note), referencing a profile-bounded irregular FOS without an obvious axis/center plane on an RMB basis may be infeasible; specify MMB/LMB, an explicit mathematical fitting routine, or datum targets where needed.
rules.pass_condition: Irregular FOS datums clearly define their boundary (MMB/LMB) or specify datum targets / explicit fitting routine if RMB.
rules.fail_condition: A complex irregular cutout controlled only by profile is referenced RMB with no datum targets or fitting routine.
rules.remediation: Reference the irregular FOS at MMB/LMB, or specify datum targets / mathematical fitting routine.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Simultaneous Requirements Default, 'SEP REQT' Override, and Composite Lower-Segment Exception
visual_syntax_triggers: Multiple Position/Profile FCFs with Identical DRF
rules.audit_check: UOS, Position and Profile tolerances located by basic dimensions to the EXACT SAME datum features in the SAME order of precedence and SAME boundary modifiers are a SIMULTANEOUS REQUIREMENT (single combined pattern). To decouple them, 'SEP REQT' SHALL be placed adjacent to each applicable FCF. Conversely, simultaneous requirement does NOT apply by default to lower segments of composite FCFs (use 'SIM REQT' to invoke it). PROHIBITED: 'SIM REQT' CANNOT be invoked across FCFs with different datum references, different precedence orders, or different boundary modifiers.
rules.pass_condition: Patterns sharing identical DRFs intentionally require simultaneous gaging (or carry 'SEP REQT'); 'SIM REQT' is used only where datum references, order, and modifiers match identically.
rules.fail_condition: 'SIM REQT' is applied to FCFs with different datum letters/order/modifiers, OR 'SEP REQT' is omitted on unrelated patterns sharing an MMB datum causing unintended simultaneous gaging cost.
rules.remediation: Remove invalid 'SIM REQT' across mismatched DRFs, and explicitly add 'SEP REQT' where independent datum shift is functionally permitted.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Restrained Condition Notes, Restraint Parameters (7.20.2), Gravity (7.20.3), and Free State Symbol (Ⓕ) Eligibility (7.20.4)
rules.audit_check: To inspect a part in a restrained state, a general note, flag, or local note SHALL define restraint requirements (7.20), referencing any external restraint document (7.20.2), and indicating gravity direction when gravity is a concern (7.20.3). PROHIBITED (7.20.4): The 'Free State' symbol (Ⓕ) MAY ONLY be applied on drawings that include one or more restraint notes! When a general note invokes restraint, all tolerances apply restrained unless overridden by Ⓕ; when a local/flag note invokes restraint, only noted tolerances apply restrained.
rules.pass_condition: Every drawing using Ⓕ contains an explicit restraint note defining magnitude/location/area/sequence (or referenced doc); restraint notes clearly specify whether global or local.
rules.fail_condition: The Free State symbol (Ⓕ) appears on a drawing that has NO restraint note (invalid per 7.20.4), OR a restraint note invokes restraint without defining how/where/how much force is applied.
rules.remediation: Either add a complete restraint note per 7.20.1–7.20.2 or remove the invalid Ⓕ symbol.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Restrained Datum Feature Contact Requirement (Non-Size Must Contact; FOS at MMB Need Not)
rules.audit_check: UOS, when restraint is applied, ALL restrained non-size datum features SHALL contact their physical datum feature simulators (unless over-constrained targets carry Ⓕ per 7.20.4.3). Features of size referenced at MMB are NOT required to contact the simulator.
rules.pass_condition: Restraint note and datum boundary conditions are physically achievable without contradicting contact requirements.
rules.fail_condition: Restraint note omits required contact exceptions on over-constrained non-size datum targets or conflicts with Ⓕ datum references.
rules.remediation: Apply Ⓕ to unrestrained datum references in over-constrained DRFs or specify explicit restraint exceptions.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: DRF Coordinate Axis Labeling ('[A,B,C]', Common Datums '[F-D,B,C]', and 3D 'DRF_XXX')
rules.audit_check: When multiple DRFs exist and coordinate axes X, Y, Z are labeled on orthographic views (7.21(a)), each labeled axis SHALL include its associated DRF in square brackets without modifiers (e.g., 'X[A,B,C]'), separating common datums by a hyphen (e.g., '[F-D,B,C]', 7.21(b)). On 3D models (7.21(c)), each DRF SHALL associate with a coordinate system and any DRF label SHALL follow the format 'DRF_XXX' (underscore required).
rules.pass_condition: Labeled multi-DRF orthographic axes include '[A,B,C]' without modifiers; 3D model DRF labels use 'DRF_XXX' with underscore.
rules.fail_condition: Multiple DRFs exist with unlabeled/ambiguous X, Y, Z axes, modifiers are illegally included inside '[AⓂ,B,C]', or 3D DRF label omits the mandatory underscore in 'DRF_XXX'.
rules.remediation: Label multi-DRF axes as 'X[A,B,C]' (no modifiers) on 2D drawings and 'DRF_ABC' (with underscore) in 3D models.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Customized DRF Requirements (2 Views Labeled, Lowercase [x,y,z,u,v,w]) & Prohibition in Composite FCFs
rules.audit_check: When a Customized Datum Reference Frame is invoked: (a) on 2D orthographic views, rectangular coordinate axes X, Y, Z SHALL be labeled in AT LEAST TWO VIEWS (once per DRF in 3D models); (b) constrained DOFs SHALL be stated in LOWERCASE letters '[x,y,z,u,v,w]' in brackets following each datum letter and modifier. PROHIBITED (7.22 Note): Customized DRFs SHALL NOT be used with composite tolerances (use one or more single-segment FCFs instead).
rules.pass_condition: Customized DRF uses lowercase [x,y,z,u,v,w] in single-segment FCFs only, and X, Y, Z coordinate axes are labeled in ≥2 orthographic views (or 1x in 3D model).
rules.fail_condition: Customized DRF appears inside a composite FCF, uses uppercase DOF letters, omits coordinate axes in ≥2 orthographic views, or constrains impossible/conflicting DOFs.
rules.remediation: Convert composite FCF to multiple single-segment FCFs, format DOF letters in lowercase '[x,y,z,u,v,w]', and label X, Y, Z axes in at least two views.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Movable Datum Target Mandatory When Non-Normal Motion + Direction Specification
rules.audit_check: Where a datum target's true geometric counterpart moves in a direction NOT normal to the true profile, the Movable Datum Target symbol SHALL be used AND the direction of movement SHALL be explicitly defined by: (a) a line element at basic angle(s) in 2D, (b) a unit vector '[i,j,k]' (with '[A,B,C]' appended if multiple DRFs exist) pointing toward the surface, or (c) an external represented line element terminating at the contact point/line/area in a 3D model.
rules.pass_condition: Every non-normal movable datum target includes the movable symbol and defines its motion vector via basic-angled line element or [i,j,k] vector.
rules.fail_condition: Movable datum target moves non-normally without defining motion direction via angled line element or [i,j,k] vector (or omits DRF tag '[A,B,C]' when multiple DRFs exist).
rules.remediation: Add the movable datum target symbol and specify movement direction via basic-angled line element or unit vector [i,j,k].

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Datum Target Location and Size Dimensions (Basic Preferred vs. Directly Toleranced)
rules.audit_check: The location and size of datum targets SHOULD be defined with either BASIC dimensions (where established tooling/gaging tolerances per ASME Y14.43 apply) or directly toleranced dimensions — never left untoleranced without basic designation.
rules.pass_condition: All datum target locations and sizes are defined by Basic dimensions (preferred) or explicit tolerances.
rules.fail_condition: Datum target coordinates appear as untoleranced dimensions on a drawing without an 'UNTOLERANCED DIMENSIONS ARE BASIC' note.
rules.remediation: Enclose datum target location and area-size dimensions in Basic dimension boxes (or enter area size inside the upper half of the target circle).

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Datum Target Point Count & Non-Collinearity for 3-2-1 Datum Planes (7.24.4, 7.24.6, 7.24.8)
rules.audit_check: A primary datum plane requires AT LEAST THREE non-collinear target points (not on a straight line); a secondary datum plane usually requires 2 targets; a tertiary plane requires 1 target (or equivalent line/area combinations). A primary datum axis (7.24.6) uses two axially separated sets of 3 equally spaced targets (with different datum letters if on two different diameters); a secondary datum axis (7.24.8) uses one set of 3 equally spaced targets.
rules.pass_condition: Target counts and geometric distribution properly constrain the intended plane/axis without collinearity or under-constraint.
rules.fail_condition: Primary datum plane has fewer than 3 target points (without line/area targets) or places 3 target points in a single straight line (collinear).
rules.remediation: Place at least 3 well-spaced non-collinear target points (or valid line/area targets) for a primary datum plane.

rules.section: Section 7: Datum Reference Frames
rules.title: Datum Targets Referenced with Fewer Than Three Mutually Perpendicular Planes
rules.audit_check: When an FCF references a datum feature defined by datum targets that themselves depend on other datums for location (e.g., referencing only datum A when A's targets are located from B and C), the basis datums SHALL be referenced OR an explicit note SHALL clarify their invocation (e.g., 'WHERE ONLY DATUM FEATURE A IS REFERENCED, DATUM FEATURES B AND C ARE INVOKED ONLY TO RELATE THE TARGETS THAT ESTABLISH DATUM A').
rules.pass_condition: FCF either references all basis datums locating the targets or includes an explicit 7.24.10 clarifying note.
rules.fail_condition: FCF references only datum A (established by targets located from B and C) with no note explaining how B and C locate the targets.
rules.remediation: Add the required 7.24.10 note clarifying how basis datums relate the datum targets.

rules.section: Section 8: Tolerances of Form
rules.title: Form Tolerances SHALL NOT Reference Datums
rules.audit_check: Form tolerances (Straightness, Flatness, Circularity, Cylindricity) apply ONLY to single features (or single features unified by 'CF') and SHALL NEVER include any datum feature reference in the Feature Control Frame.
rules.pass_condition: Every Straightness, Flatness, Circularity, and Cylindricity FCF contains ONLY the geometric symbol and tolerance compartment (zero datum compartments).
rules.fail_condition: Any datum letter (e.g., '|⏥|0.05|A|') appears inside a Straightness, Flatness, Circularity, or Cylindricity Feature Control Frame.
rules.remediation: Remove all datum references from form FCFs, or switch to an Orientation (Parallelism/Perpendicularity), Profile, or Runout symbol if datum relation is intended.

rules.section: Section 8: Tolerances of Form
rules.title: Surface Straightness — View Direction, Refinement Less Than Size Tolerance, No Ø/MMC
rules.audit_check: Surface line-element straightness (8.4.1.1, 8.4.1.2) SHALL be applied in a view where elements appear as straight lines, directed to the surface/extension line (NOT the size dimension), without Ø or Ⓜ/Ⓛ. Its tolerance value SHALL be LESS THAN the size tolerance (and any other governing geometric tolerance), EXCEPT where Ⓕ or Ⓘ overrides Rule #1.
rules.pass_condition: Surface straightness attaches to surface/extension line in a straight-element view, omits Ø and Ⓜ/Ⓛ, and has a tolerance strictly smaller than the size tolerance (unless Ⓕ or Ⓘ applies).
rules.fail_condition: Surface straightness tolerance is ≥ size tolerance (without Ⓕ/Ⓘ), includes Ø or Ⓜ/Ⓛ on a surface callout, or is placed on a circular end view of a cylinder.
rules.remediation: Move to longitudinal view, ensure tolerance < size tolerance, and remove Ø or Ⓜ/Ⓛ (or move FCF to size dimension if derived median line control is intended).

rules.section: Section 8: Tolerances of Form
rules.title: Derived Median Line Straightness — Placement on Size Dimension, Ø Prefix, and MMC vs. Orientation/Position Limit
rules.audit_check: For derived median line straightness of a cylindrical FOS: (1) FCF SHALL attach to the size dimension or dimension-line extension; (2) Ø SHALL precede the tolerance value; (3) RFS, Ⓜ, or Ⓛ may apply and Rule #1 is overridden (tolerance MAY exceed size tolerance). HOWEVER, when Straightness at Ⓜ is used with an Orientation or Position tolerance at Ⓜ, the Straightness value SHALL NOT be greater than the Orientation or Position tolerance value.
rules.pass_condition: DML straightness attaches to the size dimension, includes Ø, and (if at Ⓜ alongside orientation/position at Ⓜ) has value ≤ the orientation/position tolerance.
rules.fail_condition: DML straightness omits Ø, attaches to the surface instead of size dimension, or specifies Straightness at Ⓜ larger than Position/Orientation at Ⓜ on the same feature.
rules.remediation: Attach DML straightness directly to the size dimension, precede tolerance with Ø, and ensure Straightness Ⓜ ≤ Orientation/Position Ⓜ.

rules.section: Section 8: Tolerances of Form
rules.title: Unit-Basis Straightness & Flatness (8.4.2.2) — Total Overall Limit Recommended
visual_syntax_triggers: Unit Flatness (tol/L X W or tol/ØD)
rules.audit_check: When straightness per unit length (e.g., '0.05/25') or flatness per unit area (e.g., '0.05/25 X 25' or '0.05/Ø25') is specified, a total overall tolerance SHOULD also be specified in a stacked segment to prevent cumulative large bow/warp across the full part.
rules.pass_condition: Unit-basis straightness/flatness is paired with an overall total tolerance (or cumulative bow is explicitly non-critical).
rules.fail_condition: Unit-basis straightness or flatness appears alone on a long/large functional surface without an overall total form limit.
rules.remediation: Add an overall straightness/flatness limit in an upper segment above the per-unit refinement.

rules.section: Section 8: Tolerances of Form
rules.title: Flatness — Surface Refinement < Size Tolerance & Derived Median Plane Width Rules (8.4.2.1)
rules.audit_check: Flatness NEVER uses Ø (tolerance zone is always two parallel planes). When applied to a surface associated with a size dimension, the flatness tolerance SHALL be LESS THAN the size tolerance (unless Ⓕ or Ⓘ applies) and SHALL NOT use Ⓜ/Ⓛ. When applied to a width FOS size dimension (8.4.2.1, derived median plane), RFS/Ⓜ/Ⓛ may apply, Rule #1 is overridden, and tolerance may exceed size tolerance — still with NO Ø symbol.
rules.pass_condition: Flatness omits Ø and datums; surface flatness < size tolerance (unless Ⓕ/Ⓘ) with no Ⓜ/Ⓛ; DMP flatness attaches to width size dimension without Ø.
rules.fail_condition: Flatness includes Ø, includes a datum, applies Ⓜ/Ⓛ to a single non-FOS planar face, or has surface flatness ≥ size tolerance without Ⓕ/Ⓘ.
rules.remediation: Remove Ø/datums, verify surface flatness < size tolerance, and apply Ⓜ/Ⓛ only when attached to a width FOS size dimension.

rules.section: Section 8: Tolerances of Form
rules.title: Circularity & Cylindricity (8.4.4) — Surface Attachment Only, No Ø/MMC/LMC/Datums, and < Size Tolerance
rules.audit_check: Circularity (8.4.3) and Cylindricity (8.4.4) SHALL be applied to a SURFACE (NOT to a size dimension), SHALL NOT include Ø, Ⓜ, Ⓛ, or any datum references, and SHALL have a tolerance value LESS THAN the size tolerance (and any other governing geometric tolerances affecting roundness) — EXCEPT where Rule #1 does not apply (Ⓕ, Ⓘ, or AVG diameter for circularity per 8.5).
rules.pass_condition: Circularity/Cylindricity points directly to the surface outline, omits Ø/Ⓜ/Ⓛ/datums, and specifies a radial zone value strictly less than the size tolerance (unless Ⓕ, Ⓘ, or AVG applies).
rules.fail_condition: Circularity or Cylindricity attaches to a size dimension, includes Ø or Ⓜ/Ⓛ or datums, or has a tolerance value ≥ size tolerance without Ⓕ/Ⓘ/AVG.
rules.remediation: Attach leader directly to the surface, remove Ø/Ⓜ/Ⓛ/datums, and reduce tolerance below size tolerance (or invoke Ⓕ/Ⓘ/AVG if intended).

rules.section: Section 8: Tolerances of Form
rules.title: Average Diameter ('AVG') Rule #1 Override and Recommended Measurement Count
rules.audit_check: Qualifying a diameter with 'AVG' invokes an exception to Rule #1 (individual diametric measurements may violate size limits while the average of ≥4 measurements stays within limits) and permits circularity > size tolerance. If unrestrained circularity must be bounded, pair AVG with a Circularity tolerance.
rules.pass_condition: AVG is placed immediately after the diameter tolerance and paired with Circularity (or restrained tolerances) where free-state out-of-roundness must be limited.
rules.fail_condition: AVG is used on a rigid mating shaft/bore where local size violations would prevent assembly without intentional flexible conformance.
rules.remediation: Verify AVG is appropriate for flexible/conforming parts and pair with a Circularity limit if needed.

rules.section: Section 9: Tolerances of Orientation
rules.title: Planar Orientation Controls Flatness Automatically & Must Refine Governing Location/Size Tolerances
rules.audit_check: An orientation tolerance on a plane surface automatically controls flatness to the same tolerance (unless Ⓣ is added). Orientation does NOT control location. When refining an existing Position, Profile, or Runout tolerance to the same datum(s), the orientation tolerance SHOULD be strictly smaller than the governing location/profile/size tolerance to be meaningful.
rules.pass_condition: Refining orientation tolerances are strictly smaller than any overarching Position, Profile, Runout, or Rule #1 parallelism-via-size limits.
rules.fail_condition: An orientation refinement (e.g., ⊥ 0.5 to A) is EQUAL TO or LARGER THAN an already-applied Position (⌖ Ø0.2 to A|B|C) or Profile tolerance to the same datum A (making it redundant/nonsensical).
rules.remediation: Ensure any orientation refinement is strictly tighter than the location/profile/size control it refines, or remove the redundant FCF.

rules.section: Section 9: Tolerances of Orientation
rules.title: Orientation Tolerances SHALL Reference At Least One Datum & Use Basic Angles for Angularity
rules.audit_check: Every Orientation tolerance (Angularity, Parallelism, Perpendicularity) SHALL reference ONE OR MORE DATUMS sufficient to constrain the required rotational degrees of freedom. For Angularity (except implied 0°/90° per 9.5), the nominal angle between the considered feature and referenced datum SHALL be a BASIC angle (not a ± toleranced angle). Orientation controls ONLY rotational DOFs, never location.
rules.pass_condition: Every ∠, ∥, ⊥ FCF references valid datum(s) constraining rotation, and any non-0°/90° Angularity angle is enclosed in a Basic box (or governed by basic note).
rules.fail_condition: An Orientation FCF has NO datum reference (e.g., '|⊥|0.1|'), lacks a secondary datum needed to orient a tilted plane/axis, or pairs Angularity with a directly ± toleranced angle.
rules.remediation: Add required datum reference(s) to the Orientation FCF and convert the nominal angle for Angularity to a Basic dimension.

rules.section: Section 9: Tolerances of Orientation
rules.title: Orientation Tolerance Zone Shape (Ø for Cylindrical Axis Zone vs. No Ø for Planar/Line/Center-Plane Zone)
rules.audit_check: When an orientation tolerance controls a cylindrical feature axis perpendicular to a datum plane (or angled/parallel in 3D), Ø SHALL precede the tolerance value to create a cylindrical zone (9.3.2(b)); omitting Ø creates a two-parallel-plane zone controlling tilt in ONLY one viewing direction (9.3.2(a)). For planar surfaces, width center planes, or line elements, Ø SHALL NOT be used.
rules.pass_condition: Axis-perpendicularity to a planar datum includes Ø (unless single-direction planar zone is intentionally required); surface/width orientation omits Ø.
rules.fail_condition: Perpendicularity of a cylindrical hole/pin to a primary planar datum omits Ø unintentionally, OR Ø is placed on a planar surface orientation FCF.
rules.remediation: Add Ø for 3D cylindrical axis orientation zones and remove Ø from all planar surface or width center-plane orientation zones.

rules.section: Section 9: Tolerances of Orientation
rules.title: Prohibition of 'EACH RADIAL ELEMENT' with Orientation Tolerances (Use Profile of a Line Instead)
rules.audit_check: Adding 'EACH ELEMENT' to an orientation tolerance controls individual parallel line elements independently. HOWEVER, 'EACH RADIAL ELEMENT' invokes a translational degree of freedom that orientation tolerances CANNOT control; therefore 'EACH RADIAL ELEMENT' SHALL NOT be used with Orientation tolerances — Profile of a Line (11.9) SHALL be used instead.
rules.pass_condition: Radial surface elements are controlled via Profile of a Line (11.9), never via an Orientation FCF with 'EACH RADIAL ELEMENT'.
rules.fail_condition: An Orientation FCF (⊥, ∥, or ∠) carries the notation 'EACH RADIAL ELEMENT'.
rules.remediation: Replace the Orientation + 'EACH RADIAL ELEMENT' callout with Profile of a Line (⌒) relative to the datum plane and datum axis per 11.9.

rules.section: Section 9: Tolerances of Orientation
rules.title: Zero Orientation Tolerance at MMC/LMC and 'MAX' Bonus Cap Syntax
rules.audit_check: A zero orientation tolerance at Ⓜ (or Ⓛ) requires perfect orientation at MMC (or LMC), granting bonus tolerance only upon departure from MMC (or LMC). If full bonus tolerance must be capped, 'MAX' with the cap value SHALL follow the Ⓜ/Ⓛ modifier inside the FCF (e.g., '|⊥|Ø0Ⓜ MAX 0.1|A|'). Note (9.3.5): Orientation at Ⓜ/Ⓛ applies to all FOS EXCEPT spheres.
rules.pass_condition: Zero-at-MMC/LMC orientation FCFs include Ⓜ or Ⓛ (never bare '0' at RFS!) and format any bonus cap as 'MAX <value>' after Ⓜ/Ⓛ.
rules.fail_condition: An FCF specifies a zero tolerance WITHOUT Ⓜ or Ⓛ (impossible zero tolerance at RFS!), or applies Ⓜ/Ⓛ orientation to a spherical feature.
rules.remediation: Always pair a zero tolerance with Ⓜ or Ⓛ, place any 'MAX' cap after Ⓜ/Ⓛ, and never apply orientation to a sphere.

rules.section: Section 9: Tolerances of Orientation
rules.title: Tangent Plane Symbol (Ⓣ) Placement and Loss of Surface Form Control
rules.audit_check: When controlling only the contacting high-point tangent plane of a planar surface, Ⓣ SHALL be placed in the FCF immediately after the tolerance value (e.g., '|⊥|0.1Ⓣ|A|'). Because Ⓣ removes flatness/form control of the surface itself, audit whether surface form still needs separate flatness or size control. Ⓣ applies ONLY to planar features (not axes or curved surfaces).
rules.pass_condition: Ⓣ is placed after the tolerance value on a planar surface FCF, and lack of surface form control is acceptable or covered by a separate flatness/size control.
rules.fail_condition: Ⓣ is applied to a cylindrical axis or curved surface, placed before the tolerance value, or placed in a Form FCF (e.g., Flatness with Ⓣ is self-contradictory).
rules.remediation: Use Ⓣ only on planar surfaces in Orientation, Profile, or Runout FCFs, placed after the tolerance value.

rules.section: Section 10: Tolerances of Position
rules.title: Position Applies Strictly to Features of Size with Basic Locating Dimensions
rules.audit_check: Positional tolerancing controls the center point, axis, or center plane (or VC boundary) of FEATURES OF SIZE ONLY (holes, pins, slots, tabs, spheres, counterbores). ALL dimensions locating true position from datums and between pattern features SHALL be BASIC (10.2.1.1). PROHIBITED: Position SHALL NOT be applied to a single non-size planar surface (use Profile instead).
rules.pass_condition: Every Position FCF governs a valid feature of size (with a size tolerance) AND every linear/angular dimension locating its true position is Basic (or implied 0°/90° basic).
rules.fail_condition: Position is applied to a single planar edge/face (not a FOS), OR a dimension locating a positioned hole/slot carries a direct ± tolerance instead of a Basic box.
rules.remediation: Apply Position strictly to features of size, convert all locating dimensions to Basic, and switch single-surface location controls to Profile of a Surface.

rules.section: Section 10: Tolerances of Position
rules.title: Datum References Required for Position (Exception Only for Coaxial/Pattern Self-Relationship)
rules.audit_check: A Positional FCF SHALL reference the datum features establishing the DRF for locating dimensions — EXCEPT where a coaxial or pattern-of-features relationship has no relationship to external datums (10.6.2.3, or lower segment of a composite FCF without datums).
rules.pass_condition: Every Position FCF locating features from part boundaries includes appropriate datum feature references (unless intentionally controlling feature-to-feature self-relation only).
rules.fail_condition: A single-segment Position FCF locates a hole or pattern via basic dimensions from part edges/faces but omits all datum feature references.
rules.remediation: Identify the originating edges/faces as Datum Features and reference them in the Position FCF.

rules.section: Section 10: Tolerances of Position
rules.title: Zero Positional Tolerance Requires MMC (Ⓜ) or LMC (Ⓛ) Modifier (10.3.4, 10.3.5.3)
rules.audit_check: Positional tolerances apply RFS (default), Ⓜ, or Ⓛ. A zero positional tolerance value (0 or Ø0) is ONLY valid when modified by Ⓜ (10.3.4) or Ⓛ (10.3.5.3); a bare zero positional tolerance at RFS is physically unmanufacturable and invalid.
rules.pass_condition: Every zero positional tolerance carries Ⓜ or Ⓛ (e.g., '|⌖|Ø0Ⓜ|A|B|C|').
rules.fail_condition: Position FCF states '0' or 'Ø0' with no Ⓜ or Ⓛ modifier.
rules.remediation: Add Ⓜ (or Ⓛ) to the zero positional tolerance, or enter a nonzero RFS tolerance value.

rules.section: Section 10: Tolerances of Position
rules.title: Projected Tolerance Zone (Ⓟ) Mandatory for Threaded or Press-Fit Holes Subject to Mating Interference
rules.audit_check: The Projected Tolerance Zone (Ⓟ) SHALL be used where orientation variation of threaded holes or press-fit pin/stud holes could cause fasteners to interfere with mating parts. The specified height is a MINIMUM equal to maximum mating part thickness (for screws) or maximum installed stud/pin height (10.4.1.2, 10.4.1.3). On multiple single-segment FCFs, Ⓟ SHALL appear in all applicable segments (10.4.1); on composite FCFs, Ⓟ SHALL appear in ALL segments (10.5.1.7).
rules.pass_condition: Tapped holes and press-fit dowel holes use Ⓟ with appropriate minimum height (and in every segment of composite FCFs); assembly-level projecting studs/pins omit Ⓟ (10.4.1.3).
rules.fail_condition: A threaded or press-fit hole in a fixed-fastener pattern omits Ⓟ, OR a composite FCF places Ⓟ in only one segment instead of all segments.
rules.remediation: Add Ⓟ with minimum projection height (mating thickness or max stud/pin height) to threaded/press-fit hole Position FCFs (and to every segment of composite FCFs).

rules.section: Section 10: Tolerances of Position
rules.title: Coaxial Counterbored/Stepped Hole Positional Callouts & 'INDIVIDUALLY' Notes (10.4.2(c), 10.4.8)
rules.audit_check: When coaxial holes (e.g., hole + counterbore) share one FCF beneath both size specs, both share the same tolerance zone (10.4.2(a)); when tolerances differ, separate FCFs apply to each (10.4.2(b)). When each feature in a pattern establishes an individual datum for its own coaxial feature or local sub-pattern (10.4.2(c), 10.4.8), the SAME note (e.g., '4X INDIVIDUALLY') SHALL appear beneath/adjacent to BOTH the datum feature symbol AND the controlled FCF (or applicable segment).
rules.pass_condition: Repeated local datum/pattern relationships display matching '<N>X INDIVIDUALLY' notes on both the datum symbol and the governing FCF segment.
rules.fail_condition: 'INDIVIDUALLY' appears on the FCF without the matching note on the datum feature symbol (or vice versa), or count prefix is omitted on main views.
rules.remediation: Place matching '<N>X INDIVIDUALLY' notations adjacent to both the repeated datum feature symbol and the controlled FCF segment.

rules.section: Section 10: Tolerances of Position
rules.title: Closer Control at One End of a Long Feature (Conical Positional Tolerance Zone)
visual_syntax_triggers: Two Different Position FCFs at Opposite Hole Ends
rules.audit_check: Where two different positional tolerances are specified at opposite ends of a long hole, a conical tolerance zone is established between the two ends; each FCF MUST clearly point to its respective end surface/extremity.
rules.pass_condition: Both FCF leaders unambiguously indicate which extremity receives the tighter vs. looser tolerance.
rules.fail_condition: Two differing positional tolerances are applied to the same hole without visually distinguishing opposite ends (creating a contradiction instead of a conical zone).
rules.remediation: Point each FCF leader explicitly to its respective hole-end extremity with clear view labels.

rules.section: Section 10: Tolerances of Position
rules.title: Bidirectional & Noncircular Positional Tolerancing — Omit Diameter Symbol (Ø) (10.4.4, 10.4.5)
rules.audit_check: For bidirectional positional tolerancing of round holes (10.4.4 — rectangular or polar) and for noncircular features of size such as slots and tabs (10.4.5), the tolerance zone is NOT cylindrical; therefore the diameter symbol 'Ø' SHALL BE OMITTED from the FCF, and the direction/extent of each tolerance zone SHALL be unmistakably clear.
rules.pass_condition: Bidirectional hole FCFs and slot/tab width Position FCFs omit Ø and attach clearly in the intended direction of each parallel-plane or concentric-arc zone.
rules.fail_condition: Ø is placed in a slot/tab center-plane Position FCF or in a bidirectional rectangular/polar Position FCF.
rules.remediation: Remove Ø from bidirectional and noncircular width Position FCFs and verify clear directional attachment.

rules.section: Section 10: Tolerances of Position
rules.title: Composite Positional FCF Rules — Decreasing Tolerances, Repeated Datums Only in Exact Precedence Order
rules.audit_check: In a Composite Positional FCF: (1) the single ⌖ symbol spans all segments; (2) each lower FRTZF segment SHALL specify a strictly SMALLER tolerance than the preceding segment; (3) lower segments may omit datums OR repeat a subset of the upper segment's datums IN THE EXACT SAME ORDER OF PRECEDENCE (never introducing new datums, reordering datums, or changing boundary modifiers — those require multiple single-segment FCFs per 10.5.5); (4) lower-segment datums constrain ROTATION ONLY, never translation.
rules.pass_condition: Composite Position FCF has strictly decreasing tolerances top-to-bottom, repeats only upper-segment datums in identical precedence order/modifiers, and does not attempt translational location in the lower segment.
rules.fail_condition: Lower segment tolerance ≥ upper segment tolerance; lower segment introduces a datum not in the upper segment, reorders datums (e.g., upper A|B|C, lower B|A), changes a datum modifier, or repeats all 3 datums expecting translational control (10.5.5).
rules.remediation: Fix lower-segment datum subset/order and tolerance hierarchy, or split into multiple single-segment FCFs (10.5.2, 10.5.5) when translational constraint or different DRFs are needed.

rules.section: Section 10: Tolerances of Position
rules.title: Composite PLTZF and FRTZF Are Non-Cumulative; FRTZF Outside PLTZF Is Unusable
rules.audit_check: In composite positional (10.5.1.1 Note) and composite profile (11.6.1.1) controls, the feature SHALL simultaneously lie within BOTH the PLTZF and the FRTZF. The two zones are NOT cumulative, and any portion of the FRTZF extending outside the PLTZF is NOT usable.
rules.pass_condition: Composite PLTZF and FRTZF tolerances are verified as simultaneous containment boundaries (not added together in tolerance stackups).
rules.fail_condition: Drawing notes erroneously imply FRTZF tolerance adds on top of PLTZF tolerance.
rules.remediation: Ensure stackup and inspection notes treat PLTZF and FRTZF as simultaneously enforced, non-cumulative boundaries.

rules.section: Section 10: Tolerances of Position
rules.title: Multiple Single-Segment Positional FCFs Constrain BOTH Translation and Rotation to Lower-Segment Datums
rules.audit_check: Unlike a composite FCF (where lower-segment datums constrain rotation ONLY), in a Multiple Single-Segment Positional (or Profile, 11.7) FCF — where the ⌖ (or ⌓) symbol is repeated in each row — datum references in the lower segment constrain BOTH TRANSLATION AND ROTATION relative to those datums (and basic dimensions to those datums APPLY to the lower segment).
rules.pass_condition: Multiple single-segment FCFs are used specifically when tighter translational location to a subset of datums (e.g., |A|B|) is intended alongside a looser overall location (e.g., |A|B|C|), with lower tolerance strictly smaller than upper tolerance.
rules.fail_condition: Multiple single-segment FCF repeats the exact same full DRF |A|B|C| with a smaller tolerance in the second row (rendering the looser first row completely redundant!), OR has a looser tolerance in the lower row.
rules.remediation: Remove redundant upper segments when the full DRF is identical, or use a Composite FCF if only rotational/feature-to-feature refinement is intended.

rules.section: Section 10: Tolerances of Position
rules.title: Coaxial/Multi-Size Pattern Notation ('2X', 'nX') & Single FCF Without Datums (10.6.2.3)
rules.audit_check: Where two or more coaxial features of DIFFERENT specified sizes share the same positional tolerance (with or without datum references per 10.6.2.3), a single FCF supplemented by a count notation (such as '2X') SHALL be used (or features labeled with letters referenced beneath the FCF).
rules.pass_condition: Multi-size coaxial pattern carries a single FCF with explicit count ('2X', etc.) or letter identification clearly linking all coaxial features.
rules.fail_condition: Coaxial features of different diameters use a datum-less Position FCF without '2X' / feature identification showing which features form the coaxial group.
rules.remediation: Add explicit count notation (e.g., '2X') or feature labels beneath the shared Position FCF.

rules.section: Section 10: Tolerances of Position
rules.title: Different Datums, Precedence, or Modifiers Require Separate Single-Segment FCFs (Not Composite)
rules.audit_check: When a pattern of features requires different datum features, different datum modifiers, or the same datums in a different order of precedence, this SHALL NOT be specified as a composite FCF; separate single-segment FCFs SHALL be used.
rules.pass_condition: Separate single-segment FCFs (each with its own ⌖ symbol) are used whenever DRF letters, order, or modifiers differ between segments.
rules.fail_condition: A composite FCF attempts to change datum letters, order of precedence, or modifiers between its upper and lower segments.
rules.remediation: Convert the composite FCF into multiple single-segment FCFs (placing a separate ⌖ symbol in each row).

rules.section: Section 10: Tolerances of Position
rules.title: Selection of Coaxial & Symmetrical Controls (10.6.1, 10.7) Replacing Deleted Concentricity/Symmetry
rules.audit_check: For coaxial features (10.6.1): use Position when axis/VC with RFS/MMC/LMC applies; use Runout when controlling revolved surfaces to a datum axis; use Profile of a Surface for combined size/form/orientation/location. For symmetrical features (10.7): use Position (axis/center plane at RFS/MMC/LMC) or Profile of a Surface.
rules.pass_condition: Coaxial and symmetrical features use functionally appropriate Position, Runout, or Profile FCFs.
rules.fail_condition: A coaxial rotating bearing journal uses Position at MMC where surface roundness/runout is functionally critical (or a mating static clearance bore uses Runout where MMC bonus via Position is functionally superior).
rules.remediation: Select Position for mating FOS assemblies (especially with MMC bonus), Runout for rotating surfaces of revolution, and Profile for combined surface control.

rules.section: Section 11: Tolerances of Profile
rules.title: True Profile Must Be Defined (Basic Dimensions or CAD Data) & Size Refinement Containment
rules.audit_check: A digital CAD data file or appropriate drawing view with BASIC dimensions SHALL define the true profile for every Profile tolerance. When Profile is used as a refinement of a directly toleranced size dimension, the profile tolerance zone SHALL be contained within the size limits (unless Dynamic Profile Δ overrides size per 11.10).
rules.pass_condition: True profile geometry is fully defined via Basic dimensions or authoritative CAD model, and any size-refining profile tolerance is smaller than the size tolerance.
rules.fail_condition: Profile FCF governs a surface whose nominal geometry is defined by directly ± toleranced dimensions instead of Basic dimensions (without intending size-refinement), or refinement profile exceeds size tolerance.
rules.remediation: Define the true profile completely with Basic dimensions (or authoritative CAD model) and ensure refining profile tolerances fit within size limits.

rules.section: Section 11: Tolerances of Profile
rules.title: General Profile Tolerance Note / Block Applies to All Features UOS
rules.audit_check: When a Profile of a Surface FCF is placed in a general note or general tolerance block (e.g., 'UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED, |⌓|0.5|A|B|C| ALL OVER'), it applies to ALL features of the part UOS — including features of size unless they have overriding direct size/position tolerances or explicit exclusions.
rules.pass_condition: General profile note explicitly pairs with an 'UNTOLERANCED DIMENSIONS ARE BASIC' note (or CAD model authority) and does not conflict with active general ± linear tolerance tables.
rules.fail_condition: A general All-Over Profile FCF note coexists alongside an active general ± linear/angular tolerance block in the title block, creating double-tolerancing conflict on every feature.
rules.remediation: Remove/void the general ± linear/angular tolerance block when a general All-Over Profile tolerance governs the drawing.

rules.section: Section 11: Tolerances of Profile
rules.title: Profile Sharp Corners & Rate-of-Change/Blend Clarification
rules.audit_check: Where a profile tolerance encompasses a sharp corner, the tolerance zone extends to the intersection of boundary lines, permitting rounding of the actual corner. Where abrupt undulations or corner rounding is undesirable, the drawing SHALL explicitly specify design requirements (e.g., maximum corner radius or blend/rate-of-change requirement).
rules.pass_condition: Functional sharp edges or smooth aerodynamic/sealing blends under broad profile zones include explicit max radius or blend/surface-waviness constraints.
rules.fail_condition: A large All-Around profile tolerance encompasses a functionally critical sharp sealing edge without specifying a max corner radius.
rules.remediation: Add an explicit maximum corner radius (e.g., 'R0.2 MAX') or blend requirement where profile zone corner rounding is unacceptable.

rules.section: Section 11: Tolerances of Profile
rules.title: Bilateral Profile Leader Placement & Unequally Disposed (Ⓤ) Syntax (11.3.1.2)
