rules.audit_check: A Profile FCF leader SHALL be directed to the surface or surface extension line — NEVER to a basic dimension (11.3.1.1). Unilateral or unequally disposed profile tolerances SHALL use the Ⓤ modifier followed by a second value indicating the tolerance ADDING material (outside the part): e.g., '0.3 Ⓤ 0.3' (all adding material), '0.3 Ⓤ 0' (all removing material), '0.3 Ⓤ 0.1' (0.1 adding, 0.2 removing). The second value SHALL NOT exceed the total tolerance value unless intentionally shifted completely outside the profile (and must be unambiguously verified).
rules.pass_condition: Profile FCF leader points to the surface/extension line (never a basic dimension), and any Ⓤ symbol is followed by the exact material-added portion value.
rules.fail_condition: Profile FCF leader points directly to a Basic Dimension Box, OR Ⓤ appears without its second numeric value, OR legacy phantom-line unilateral arrows are used ambiguously instead of Ⓤ.
rules.remediation: Attach Profile FCF leaders strictly to the surface/extension line and specify unilateral/unequal zones using '<total> Ⓤ <material-added>'.

rules.section: Section 11: Tolerances of Profile
rules.title: Prohibition of 'All Around' (○) in 2D Axonometric Views & Defining Profile Extent (11.3.1.4, 11.3.1.5)
rules.audit_check: PROHIBITED (11.3.1.3): The 'All Around' symbol SHALL NOT be applied in an axonometric (isometric/trimetric) view on a 2D drawing. Where different segments of a profile have different tolerances (or transition to directly toleranced segments), the exact extent of each profile tolerance SHALL be indicated (e.g., reference letters + '↔' Between symbol, 11.3.1.4). All Over (11.3.1.5) SHALL be applied via the All Over symbol, 'ALL OVER' beneath the FCF, or a general note/tolerance block.
rules.pass_condition: All Around appears strictly in orthographic views; segmented profiles clearly mark boundary letters with '↔'; All Over uses one of the 3 valid methods.
rules.fail_condition: All Around circle appears in a 2D isometric view, OR two conflicting profile tolerances meet on a continuous contour without '↔' boundary letters.
rules.remediation: Move All Around to an orthographic view (or use All Over), and bound adjacent differing profile zones with labeled extremity letters and '↔'.

rules.section: Section 11: Tolerances of Profile
rules.title: Nonuniform Profile Tolerance Zone ('NONUNIFORM' & From-To '→' Syntax)
rules.audit_check: For a smoothly transitioning nonuniform profile zone, specify start-to-end widths with '→' (e.g., '0.1 → 0.3' with 'S → T' below FCF) or place 'NONUNIFORM' in the tolerance compartment when boundaries are defined by CAD data or basic phantom-line boundaries (11.3.2.3). The extent of each nonuniform segment SHALL be clearly identified with extremity reference letters (11.3.2.1).
rules.pass_condition: Nonuniform profile callout clearly identifies extremity letters, transition direction ('S → T'), and either start/end values or CAD/phantom-line boundaries.
rules.fail_condition: 'NONUNIFORM' appears in an FCF without CAD boundary data or basic phantom-line zone definitions, or omits extremity letters.
rules.remediation: Add extremity labels with '→' transition values or explicitly define CAD/phantom-line boundaries for 'NONUNIFORM'.

rules.section: Section 11: Tolerances of Profile
rules.title: Coplanar Surfaces (Datum-Less Profile + Count) & Offset Surfaces (Basic Offset, 11.4.1.2)
rules.audit_check: To control coplanarity of two or more separated coplanar surfaces (11.4.1.1), apply a datum-less Profile of a Surface FCF with a clear count/association (e.g., '2X' or '4 SURFACES' or 'CF'). To control offset parallel surfaces (11.4.1.2), apply a Profile of a Surface FCF spanning both surfaces with a BASIC offset dimension between them.
rules.pass_condition: Coplanar/offset surfaces clearly indicate all included faces (e.g., '2X', 'CF', multiple leaders) and use Basic offset dimensions where stepped.
rules.fail_condition: Flatness (instead of Profile) is mistakenly applied across two separated coplanar pads without 'CF', OR an offset step between two surfaces controlled by one Profile FCF uses a ± dimension instead of a Basic dimension.
rules.remediation: Use Profile of a Surface with explicit surface count (or Flatness with 'CF') for coplanar surfaces, and use Basic dimensions for offset steps.

rules.section: Section 11: Tolerances of Profile
rules.title: Profile Applied to a Non-Size Datum Feature (Unilateral Into Material Only)
rules.audit_check: When a non-size datum feature is controlled by a profile tolerance that references ITSELF (e.g., All Over profile relative to |A|B|C|): (a) for equal bilateral profile, only HALF the tolerance is available on datum A (since the datum cannot penetrate the datum plane); (b) for unilateral profile, the tolerance MAY ONLY be applied INTO THE MATERIAL ('Ⓤ 0', never adding material outside the datum plane).
rules.pass_condition: Profile encompassing a non-size datum either uses bilateral (understanding half-zone at the datum) or unilateral into-material ('Ⓤ 0').
rules.fail_condition: A unilateral outside-material ('Ⓤ <full>') profile tolerance is applied to a non-size datum feature referencing itself (geometrically impossible since high points establish the datum plane).
rules.remediation: Use unilateral into-material ('Ⓤ 0'), equal bilateral, or separate flatness/form control on the datum feature itself.

rules.section: Section 11: Tolerances of Profile
rules.title: Prohibition of MMC (Ⓜ) and LMC (Ⓛ) on Profile Tolerance Values
rules.audit_check: Because Profile is a surface control, MMC (Ⓜ) and LMC (Ⓛ) modifiers SHALL NOT be applied to the tolerance value in any Profile of a Surface or Profile of a Line FCF. (MMB Ⓜ and LMB Ⓛ are permissible ONLY on eligible datum feature references.)
rules.pass_condition: No Profile FCF contains Ⓜ or Ⓛ in its tolerance compartment (only in valid datum reference compartments).
rules.fail_condition: Ⓜ or Ⓛ appears next to the tolerance value inside a Profile of a Surface or Profile of a Line FCF (e.g., '|⌓|0.2Ⓜ|A|B|C|').
rules.remediation: Remove Ⓜ/Ⓛ from the Profile tolerance compartment (keep Ⓜ/Ⓛ only on valid secondary/tertiary FOS datum references).

rules.section: Section 11: Tolerances of Profile
rules.title: Composite Profile FCF Rules, 'INDIVIDUALLY' Size/Form Refinement (11.6.2), and Prohibition of DRF Changes (11.6.1.3(c))
rules.audit_check: In a Composite Profile FCF: (1) each lower segment SHALL specify a strictly smaller tolerance than the preceding segment; (2) lower segments may omit datums or repeat a subset of upper-segment datums in IDENTICAL precedence order (constraining rotation only); (3) where different datums, modifiers, or precedence order are needed, multiple single-segment FCFs SHALL be used (NEVER composite, 11.6.1.3(c)); (4) when an independent single-segment 'INDIVIDUALLY' profile controls size/form beneath a composite profile (11.6.2), its tolerance SHALL be LESS THAN the lower FRTZF segment.
rules.pass_condition: Composite Profile has strictly decreasing tolerances, valid repeated-datum subsets, and any 'INDIVIDUALLY' refinement is strictly tighter than the FRTZF.
rules.fail_condition: Composite Profile changes/reorders datums or modifiers in lower segments, has non-decreasing tolerances, or has an 'INDIVIDUALLY' profile ≥ the FRTZF tolerance.
rules.remediation: Correct datum subset/order and tolerance progression, or convert to multiple single-segment Profile FCFs.

rules.section: Section 11: Tolerances of Profile
rules.title: Combined Profile + Position ('BOUNDARY') Control for Noncylindrical Irregular Features
rules.audit_check: Where a Profile FCF controls the shape/size of a noncylindrical irregular feature and a stacked Position FCF (at MMC/LMC, optional 'BOUNDARY' note beneath) locates its VC boundary, the Position FCF SHALL omit Ø and its boundary equals the profile MMC ± positional tolerance.
rules.pass_condition: Combined Profile + Position on an irregular cutout/boss omits Ø on the Position FCF and defines the basic profile unambiguously.
rules.fail_condition: Combined Profile + Position on a noncylindrical cutout includes Ø in the Position FCF.
rules.remediation: Omit Ø in the stacked Position FCF on noncylindrical irregular features and optionally add 'BOUNDARY' beneath it for clarity.

rules.section: Section 11: Tolerances of Profile
rules.title: Profile of a Line (⌒) Orientation & Cross-Sectional Refinement Interpretation
rules.audit_check: Profile of a Line (⌒) controls individual 2D cross-sectional line elements independently (NOT the full 3D surface). When used as a refinement of a Profile of a Surface or size tolerance, its tolerance value SHALL be strictly smaller than the overarching Profile of a Surface or size tolerance, and the viewing plane / cross-section direction SHALL be unmistakably clear.
rules.pass_condition: Profile of a Line is strictly tighter than any governing Profile of a Surface/size tolerance and applied in a view that clearly shows the controlled cross-sectional elements.
rules.fail_condition: Profile of a Line is used alone where full 3D surface control is needed, has a tolerance ≥ overarching Profile of a Surface, or leaves cross-section direction ambiguous.
rules.remediation: Ensure Profile of a Line is strictly smaller than overarching surface/size tolerances and clearly define the section orientation (or switch to Profile of a Surface).

rules.section: Section 11: Tolerances of Profile
rules.title: Dynamic Profile Tolerance Modifier (Δ) — Form-Only Refinement Independent of Size
rules.audit_check: The Dynamic Profile modifier (Δ) is valid ONLY on a refining Profile tolerance (lower segment of a composite or multiple single-segment Profile FCF, strictly smaller than the overarching static Profile or size tolerance) to control form (and orientation/location if datums apply) INDEPENDENT OF SIZE. It SHALL NOT be used as a standalone sole control with no overarching size/static-profile limit.
rules.pass_condition: Δ appears on a smaller refining Profile segment paired with a larger static Profile (or size) tolerance that bounds overall size.
rules.fail_condition: Δ is applied to a non-Profile geometric symbol, used as the sole size-unbounded profile tolerance on a feature, or specifies a value ≥ the overarching static profile tolerance.
rules.remediation: Use Δ strictly on a tighter refining Profile segment beneath an overarching static Profile or size tolerance.

rules.section: Section 11: Tolerances of Profile
rules.title: Dynamic Profile (Δ) Multiple Features Treated as Single Feature Unless 'INDIVIDUALLY' Specified
rules.audit_check: Per 11.10.3 Note, when Dynamic Profile (Δ) applies to multiple features, all features are treated as a SINGLE feature progressing uniformly together UNLESS the term 'INDIVIDUALLY' follows a separate single-segment profile FCF.
rules.pass_condition: Multi-feature Dynamic Profile either intends simultaneous uniform progression across all features or adds 'INDIVIDUALLY' on a separate single-segment FCF.
rules.fail_condition: Multiple independent features carry a shared Δ profile FCF without 'INDIVIDUALLY' when each feature must expand/contract independently.
rules.remediation: Add 'INDIVIDUALLY' adjacent to a separate single-segment Dynamic Profile FCF if independent feature progression is required.

rules.section: Section 12: Tolerances of Runout
rules.title: Runout Applicability (Surfaces Around or Perpendicular to a Datum Axis), Mandatory Datum, and Prohibition of Ø / Ⓜ / Ⓛ
rules.audit_check: Runout tolerances (Circular ↗ and Total ⌰) apply ONLY to surfaces of revolution constructed around a datum axis OR planar surfaces perpendicular to a datum axis. Every Runout FCF SHALL reference a datum axis (or cylindrical + perpendicular face datums, or assembly axis of rotation per 12.6.8). PROHIBITED: Runout FCFs SHALL NOT contain Ø, Ⓜ, or Ⓛ in EITHER the tolerance compartment OR the datum feature reference compartments (5.9.1 Note, 6.6, 7.12.2 — Runout is ALWAYS RFS and RMB only!).
rules.pass_condition: Runout applies to a valid coaxial/perpendicular surface of revolution/face, references an axis-establishing datum, and contains ZERO Ø, Ⓜ, or Ⓛ symbols anywhere in the FCF.
rules.fail_condition: Runout has no datum reference, includes Ø before the tolerance, includes Ⓜ or Ⓛ on either the tolerance OR any datum reference, or is applied to a non-revolved/oblique flat feature.
rules.remediation: Remove all Ø, Ⓜ, and Ⓛ modifiers from the Runout FCF, verify a valid datum axis is referenced, and ensure the feature is coaxial with or perpendicular to that axis.

rules.section: Section 12: Tolerances of Runout
rules.title: Runout Datum Axis Establishment (Sufficient Length, Coaxial Common Datums, or Cylinder + Perpendicular Face)
rules.audit_check: The datum axis for a Runout tolerance SHOULD be established by: (1) a single cylindrical datum feature of sufficient length, (2) two axially separated cylindrical datum features as a common datum (e.g., '|A-B|', 12.6.2), or (3) a cylindrical datum combined with a perpendicular face in order of precedence (e.g., '|A|B|', 12.6.3). Where datum surface form is critical (12.6.4), cylindricity/flatness/circularity SHALL be specified on the datum feature(s).
rules.pass_condition: Runout datum axis is stably established by a long cylinder, separated common bearing journals (A-B), or face + cylinder, with appropriate form control on datum features.
rules.fail_condition: Runout references a very short/thin cylindrical boss alone (unable to stabilize axis tilt) without a perpendicular face or second coaxial bearing datum.
rules.remediation: Establish the runout datum axis using two separated bearing diameters (A-B) or a perpendicular face + cylinder.

rules.section: Section 12: Tolerances of Runout
rules.title: Intended Surface Interruptions Excluded From Runout & Common Multi-Leader Runout (12.7)
rules.audit_check: Intended surface interruptions (such as keyways, cross-holes, or grooves) do NOT affect runout zone boundaries, which apply only where material exists (12.4). Multiple leaders from a single Runout FCF may point to two or more surfaces sharing a common runout tolerance without coupling them into a single envelope unless Total Runout on coplanar/equal-diameter surfaces is intended (12.7). Runout may also apply to a datum feature relative to its own derived axis (12.6.5) or at assembly level to a labeled axis of rotation (12.6.8).
rules.pass_condition: Multi-leader runout callouts and assembly-level runout callouts clearly designate their controlled surfaces and datum axis / axis of rotation.
rules.fail_condition: Assembly-level runout omits axis-of-rotation identification where datums only orient (not locate) the rotating axis (12.6.8).
rules.remediation: Label the axis of rotation clearly on assembly-level runout drawings and verify multi-leader target surfaces.

rules.section: Section 12: Tolerances of Runout
rules.title: Total Runout Restricted to Cylinders and Perpendicular Planes (Not Cones/Curved Surfaces)
rules.audit_check: Circular Runout (12.4.1) may be applied to cylindrical, conical, curved surfaces of revolution, and perpendicular planar faces. Total Runout (12.4.2.1, 12.4.2.2) applies ONLY to cylindrical surfaces around a datum axis or planar faces perpendicular to a datum axis (use Circular Runout or Profile of a Surface for cones and curved revolved surfaces).
rules.pass_condition: Total Runout (⌰) is applied exclusively to cylindrical surfaces or faces perpendicular to the datum axis.
rules.fail_condition: Total Runout (⌰) is applied to a conical taper or curved spherical/toroidal surface.
rules.remediation: Replace Total Runout on conical or curved revolved surfaces with Circular Runout (↗) or Profile of a Surface (⌓).

rules.section: Section 12: Tolerances of Runout
rules.title: Partial Surface Runout Requires Chain Line or 'Between' Symbol with Basic Dimensions
rules.audit_check: Where a runout tolerance applies to only a partial axial length of a surface, a chain line (on one side of the datum axis) or the 'between' symbol SHALL define the extent, located and dimensioned with BASIC dimensions from a datum reference frame (12.4.1(a), 12.4.3).
rules.pass_condition: Partial-surface runout uses a chain line or '↔' symbol with Basic dimensions locating its axial extent from the DRF.
rules.fail_condition: Partial runout chain line lacks basic location/extent dimensions from the DRF.
rules.remediation: Dimension the partial runout zone's location and length with Basic dimensions from the referenced datum.

rules.section: Section 12: Tolerances of Runout
rules.title: Runout vs. Size Tolerance Interaction (Radial Runout Limits Diameter Variation to 2× Runout)
rules.audit_check: Unlike surface form tolerances, Runout MAY be greater than, equal to, or less than the size tolerance (12.3, 12.5). Note that a small runout tolerance T limits diametric variation (circularity at each cross section for circular runout 12.5.1, or across the whole cylinder for total runout 12.5.2) to at most 2T.
rules.pass_condition: Runout and size tolerance values are functionally compatible and do not unintentionally over-restrict manufacturing cost.
rules.fail_condition: A tight total runout tolerance unintentionally contradicts a much looser functional taper/size requirement (or vice versa).
rules.remediation: Verify whether Circular Runout (allows taper within size limits) or Total Runout (restricts taper to 2× runout) matches functional intent.

rules.section: Section 12: Tolerances of Runout
rules.title: Runout Applied to a Tangent Plane — Circular Extent Default
rules.audit_check: UOS, when Runout is applied with a Tangent Plane modifier (Ⓣ) to coplanar face(s) perpendicular to an axis of rotation, the tangent plane extent is a circle with radius equal to the distance from the axis of rotation to the furthest point on the toleranced surface(s).
rules.pass_condition: Runout + Ⓣ is applied only to planar face(s) perpendicular to the datum axis (not cylinders), and circular extent matches functional mating.
rules.fail_condition: Ⓣ is combined with Runout on a cylindrical surface (invalid — tangent plane applies only to planar faces).
rules.remediation: Apply Runout + Ⓣ strictly to planar faces perpendicular to the datum axis.

rules.section: Mandatory Appendix I & Nonmandatory Appendix D: Alternative and Former Practices
rules.title: No Defined Meaning for Directly Applied ± Location Tolerances on Regular Features of Size
rules.audit_check: Directly applied ± tolerances on dimensions locating regular features of size (holes, pins, slots, bosses) were REMOVED from ASME Y14.5 in 1982 and have NO DEFINED MEANING in ASME Y14.5-2018 (not even as an alternative practice). Regular features of size SHALL be located using Basic dimensions + Position, Profile, or Runout tolerances (Sections 10, 11, 12).
rules.pass_condition: Zero regular features of size are located by direct ± coordinate tolerances.
rules.fail_condition: Holes, pins, counterbores, or slots are located by directly toleranced ± linear/polar coordinate dimensions (e.g., '25.0 ±0.1' to a hole center).
rules.remediation: Convert hole/pin/slot locating dimensions to Basic dimensions and add a Position FCF relative to an explicit DRF.

rules.section: Mandatory Appendix I & Nonmandatory Appendix D: Alternative and Former Practices
rules.title: Ambiguity Warning for Directly Applied ± Location Tolerances Between Surfaces (I-2.2, I-2.3, I-3)
rules.audit_check: While Mandatory Appendix I allows directly applied ± location tolerances on planar surfaces as a legacy alternative practice, it creates measurement-origin and measurement-vector ambiguity when surfaces vary in form/orientation (I-2.2) and worsens tolerance stackup in chain dimensioning (I-2.1). Per I-2.3 and I-3, the user is responsible for eliminating ambiguity; preferred practice is Basic location dimensions + Profile tolerances (and Basic angles + Orientation tolerances).
rules.pass_condition: Critical planar surface steps and angles use Basic dimensions with Profile/Orientation FCFs (or unambiguously specify origin/vector if using Appendix I).
rules.fail_condition: Complex multi-step surfaces or critical mating angles rely on chain ± dimensions without origin symbols or GD&T profile/orientation controls.
rules.remediation: Replace ambiguous ± surface-location and ± angular dimensions with Basic dimensions and Profile/Orientation FCFs.

rules.section: Mandatory Appendix I & Nonmandatory Appendix D: Alternative and Former Practices
rules.title: Deleted Former Symbols: Concentricity (◎), Symmetry (⌯), Legacy RFS (Ⓢ), and Legacy Boxed Datum (-A-)
rules.audit_check: Per Nonmandatory Appendix D (D-2, D-3, D-4) and prior revisions, the Concentricity (◎) and Symmetry (⌯) symbols have been DELETED from ASME Y14.5-2018 (along with obsolete Ⓢ RFS symbol and legacy '-A-' datum frame). None of these deprecated symbols SHALL appear on a drawing referencing ASME Y14.5-2018.
rules.pass_condition: Drawing uses strictly active ASME Y14.5-2018 symbols (12 geometric characteristics, Rule #2 implicit RFS/RMB, triangle-based datum feature symbols).
rules.fail_condition: Drawing citing ASME Y14.5-2018 contains ◎ (Concentricity), ⌯ (Symmetry), Ⓢ (RFS), or legacy '-A-' datum frames.
rules.remediation: Replace ◎ with Position, Runout, or Profile; replace ⌯ with Position or Profile; remove Ⓢ; update '-A-' frames to standard triangle-attached datum feature symbols.
